<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We prove $`\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}`$, resolving the derandomization problem for polynomial-time randomized logarithmic space.

- **claim-logspace-equality** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-main)): $$\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}.$$
  - Explanation: The paper asserts equality of deterministic logarithmic space and both bounded-error randomized logarithmic-space classes.
- **claim-unary-probability-approximation** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-thm-probability)): Fix a randomized machine $\mathcal M$ with polynomial worst-case running time and $O(\log(n+2))$ work space. Let $p_{\mathcal M}(x)$ be its acceptance probability on an input $x$ of length $n$. There is a uniform deterministic algorithm which, on input $(x,1^q)$ with $q\ge1$, outputs an integer $0\le a\le2^{q+2}$ satisfying $$\left\|a2^{-(q+2)}-p_{\mathcal M}(x)\right\|\le2^{-q}.$$ It uses $O(\log(n+2)+q)$ work space and $(n+2)^{O(1)}2^{O(q)}$ time. The constants depend only on $\mathcal M$.
  - Explanation: A uniform deterministic estimator separates input storage from requested precision; its time dependence on precision is exponential.
- **claim-configuration-reduction** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-model-reduction)): Fix a polynomial-time randomized machine using $O(\log(n+2))$ work space. On an input of length $n$ one can specify, uniformly in logarithmic space, a polynomial-size vertex set $V_0$, a strictly forward substochastic matrix $S$, a vector $e\in\{0,1\}^{V_0}$, and a start vertex $x_0$ with the following properties.* 1. *The incoming and outgoing port degrees of $S$ are bounded by constants depending only on the machine. Port validity, edge weights, and pairing are computable in logarithmic space.* 2. *The vector $p_0=(I-S)^{-1}e$ is well defined and belongs to $[0,1]^{V_0}$.* 3. *The coordinate $p_0(x_0)$ is the acceptance probability of the machine.* *In particular, an $\mathsf{RL}$ computation gives the promise $p_0(x_0)=0$ or $p_0(x_0)\ge1/2$.
  - Explanation: Time-layered configurations provide bounded paired ports and a finite inverse whose designated coordinate is the acceptance probability.
- **claim-rank-channel-estimates** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-env-ranks)): There are positive constants $c_\pi,C_\pi,C_{\rm pair},C_{\rm var}$, depending only on $H,h_0$, with the following properties in every admissible finite range.* 1. *A specified identifier is retained at rate $a$ with probability $\pi_a$, where $c_\pi a\le\pi_a\le C_\pi a$.* 2. *For distinct identifiers $x,y$ and any admissible rates $u,a$, $$\Pr\{X_a(y)=1\mid X_u(x)=1\}\le C_{\rm pair}a.$$* 3. *If $A_0$ is a deterministic set of $q$ distinct identifiers and $T_a=\sum_{y\in A_0}X_a(y)$, then $$\Pr\{T_a<q\pi_a/2\}\le \frac{C_{\rm var}}{q\pi_a} \quad(q>0).$$* 4. *Replacing every channel argument $y$ by the same injective affine map $\alpha y+\beta$ leaves the joint law of all evaluations unchanged, provided $\alpha\ne0$ in $\mathbb F_P$. In particular, a common fixed padding suffix leaves their law unchanged.
  - Explanation: Frame-conditioned rank channels provide comparable marginal rates, conditional pair bounds, a lower-tail estimate and affine invariance.
- **claim-forward-fixed-point-truncation** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-hier-fixed-point)): For every fixed column multiplier $0\leq g\leq1$, there is a unique strictly forward nonnegative solution of $$E_*(x,y)=fQ((C+E_*C)(x,y)/f)g(y). \label{eq:hier-fixed-point}$$ For the recurrence in Equation <a href="#eq:hier-fixed-g-iteration" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:hier-fixed-g-iteration">[eq:hier-fixed-g-iteration]</a>, $0\leq E_i\leq E_*$, and for every $k\geq0$, $$\max_{x,y}\frac{E_*(x,y)-E_k(x,y)}f \leq e^{1/\theta_1}\frac{(L_Q/\theta_1)^k}{k!}. \label{eq:hier-factorial}$$ In particular $k_*$ can be chosen as a fixed integer so that the right side of Equation <a href="#eq:hier-factorial" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:hier-factorial">[eq:hier-factorial]</a> at $k=k_*$ is at most $q^{-1}/32$, uniformly in $C,f,V$, and $g$.
  - Explanation: Strict ordering gives a unique comparison fixed point and a factorial truncation bound uniform over the stage universe.
- **claim-pilot-actual-domination** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-hier-pilot-bounds)): All pilot and actual inputs and corrections are nonnegative and strictly forward. For $1\leq i\leq k_*$, $$\begin{aligned} G_i\mathbf 1,\ \widehat E_i\mathbf 1, \ G'_i\mathbf 1,\ E_i\mathbf 1&\leq i\mathbf 1,\\ G_i(x,y),\ \widehat E_i(x,y), \ G'_i(x,y),\ E_i(x,y)&\leq if. \end{aligned}$$ Moreover, $$E_{i-1}\leq E_i\leq\widehat E_i, \qquad G'_i\leq G_i.$$ The row and column supports of every matrix in this statement are contained in $\mathcal R(C)$ and $\mathcal T(C)$, respectively.
  - Explanation: Pilot bounds dominate the monotone actual recurrence while preserving forward support and controlling entry sizes and row mass.
- **claim-overloaded-column-detection** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-hier-column-test)): Let $$D_{\rm row}=1+C_{\rm pair}k_*/\eta_-.$$ Choose the integer $K\geq160D_{\rm row}$, increasing it if necessary for the other finitely many row-gate estimates. For any fixed positive integer $J$, choose $$R_*\geq c_\pi^{-1}\max(4J,40C_{\rm var}). \label{eq:hier-column-constants}$$ Then the pilot has the following properties.* 1. *If $\#\{x:G_i(x,y)\geq\delta_1f\}>R_*/f$, then $U_i(y)\geq19/20>9/10$.* 2. *If $U_i(y)>1/4$, then $$\#\{x:G_i(x,y)>\delta_0f\} >\frac{J}{4C_\pi f}.$$* 3. *For any pilot correction with multiplier $\widehat g_i(y)>0$, $$\#\{x:G_i(x,y)\geq\delta_1f\}\leq R_*/f.$$ For every actual correction, $g(y)>0$ implies $$\#\{x:G'_i(x,y)\geq\delta_1f\}\leq R_*/f.$$
  - Explanation: Detector expectations distinguish overloaded columns and bound the substantial-entry support wherever correction remains enabled.
- **claim-finite-residual-domination** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-hier-residual)): For the $k_*$ chosen in Lemma <a href="#lem:hier-fixed-point" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:hier-fixed-point">5</a>, put $$K_*=k_*+1,\qquad \varepsilon_{\rm good}=\theta_2+q^{-1}/32<q^{-1}/16, \qquad c_{\rm dom}=\theta_1/(2k_*).$$ The matrix $D$ in Equation <a href="#eq:hier-residual-definition" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:hier-residual-definition">[eq:hier-residual-definition]</a> is nonnegative, strictly forward, and substochastic. Its entries satisfy $$D(x,y)\leq K_*f, \qquad g(y)=1\ \Longrightarrow\ D(x,y)\leq\varepsilon_{\rm good}f. \label{eq:hier-residual-entry-bounds}$$ Furthermore, $$D\geq c_{\rm dom}(C+E+EC). \label{eq:hier-domination}$$ Thus every unsigned term in $C-E+EC$ is bounded by a fixed multiple of $D$. In the formulas $G_i=C+\widehat E_{i-1}C$ and $G'_i=C+E_{i-1}C$, each unsigned term is bounded by the corresponding input itself. Moreover, $\mathcal R(D)\subseteq\mathcal R(C)$ and $\mathcal T(D)\subseteq\mathcal T(C)$.
  - Explanation: The finite residual remains substochastic and dominates its unsigned constituents, permitting separate error charges despite subtraction.
- **claim-copy-density-reduction** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-hier-copy-step)): Choose the detector rank $J$ large enough that $$J\geq\frac{2C_\pi(D_0-1)k_*(k_*+1)}{\delta_0}, \label{eq:hier-active-J}$$ and then choose $R_*$ as in Equation <a href="#eq:hier-column-constants" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:hier-column-constants">[eq:hier-column-constants]</a>. The matrix $C^+$ is strictly forward and substochastic, and $$C^+(x_i,y_j)\leq f/q, \qquad \|\mathcal A(C^+)\|\leq2\|\mathcal A(C)\|.$$ If $P^r$ is the matrix from $V^+$ to $V$ defined by $$P^r(x_i,x)=r_i(x),\qquad P^r(x_i,z)=0\quad(z\ne x), \label{eq:hier-projection}$$ then $$C^+P^r=P^rD. \label{eq:hier-one-step-intertwining}$$
  - Explanation: Destination routing reduces entry density, controls active copies and preserves the weighted projection identity.
- **claim-reward-transport-target** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-hier-reward-target)): For every stage, $$C_lP_l^c=P_l^c-B_l(I-S). \label{eq:hier-reward-algebra}$$ The vectors $W_l=B_le$ satisfy $$0\leq W_l\leq1,\qquad W_l=P_l^cp_0-C_lP_l^cp_0, \label{eq:hier-reward-bound}$$ and their updates are $$W_{l+1}(x_i)=r_i(x)\bigl(W_l(x)+(E_lW_l)(x)\bigr). \label{eq:hier-reward-update}$$ If $\bar x_l$ is the all-primary copy of a base vertex $x$, then $$0\leq p_0(x)-W_l(\bar x_l) \leq \|V_0\|\,2^{-(H-1)l}. \label{eq:hier-final-error}$$ Consequently there is $L=O(B)$ for which the last upper bound is strictly less than $1/16$ for every base vertex $x$. In particular, $p_0(x)=0$ implies $W_L(\bar x_L)=0$, and $p_0(x)\ge1/2$ implies $W_L(\bar x_L)>7/16$. Every full stage domain has size $2^{O(B)}$ and admits $O(B)$-bit addresses.
  - Explanation: Cumulative projections transport rewards so that primary copies approximate every original acceptance probability with a decaying residual.
- **claim-dense-atom-normalization** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-atom-dense)): For sufficiently large fixed $K$, the table $$\mathcal B_a(x,y)= \mathbf1_{\{Y_t(y)=1\}}\frac{k_a(d_y)R}{c(q_y)} \label{eq:atom-dense-table}$$ on retained starts has bounded values and row support. On the slice $X_u(x)=Y_t(y)=1$ its conditional expectation times $a$ equals $G(x,y)\omega_k(G(x,y))$. The same assertion holds for $\mathcal B_a^{(j)}$ with the routing fraction included. Apart from its start membership, its true value uses only the terminal channel.
  - Explanation: Preparatory normalization restores the exact bin mean while row gates keep each sampled row bounded.
- **claim-fine-product-mass** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-hier-bin-products)): Let $C$ be the transition matrix at the current stage, and let $F$ be any finite pilot or actual correction there. If a matrix $A_b\geq0$ on the same vertex set satisfies $A_b\mathbf 1\leq\mathbf 1$ and $A_b(x,y)\leq c_b b$ for some $b>0$, then $$(FA_b)\mathbf 1\leq k_*\mathbf 1, \qquad (FA_b)(x,y)\leq k_*c_b b.$$ If also $A_b\leq C$, then $FA_b\leq FC$. These estimates have constants independent of the bin scale $b$.
  - Explanation: A finite correction preserves scale-sensitive entry and row-mass bounds when multiplied by a deterministic bin contribution.
- **claim-correction-atom-normalization** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-atom-correction)): For sufficiently large fixed $K$ and then $K_c$, the conditional mean of $f\mathcal F(x,y)$ on $X_u(x)=Y_t(y)=1$ is exactly $F(x,y)$. On a true position with $Q(d_y)>0$ and $g_0(y)>0$, $$q_y=\alpha(x,y):= \mathbb E[R T_y\mid X_u(x)=Y_t(y)=1]\ge3/4. \label{eq:atom-alpha-bound}$$ No lower bound on $q_y$ or $\alpha(x,y)$ is required when $g_0(y)=0$. The true gates and normalization use only the two role channels $X,Y$; $g_0$ is deterministic.
  - Explanation: Joint row and incoming gates recover the exact correction mean; zero column multipliers require no positive normalization mean.
- **claim-support-margins** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-atom-margins)): Suppose a bounded nonnegative main function $k(v)$ vanishes for $v\le\vartheta$. Its product $k(v)R_{\vartheta}(\rho)$ and the preparatory product $h_{\vartheta}(v)R_{\vartheta}(\rho)$ have at most $K-1$ nonzero real entries in a row. They admit a common exposed class $A$, of at most $K-1$ real entries, containing their supports and satisfying $I_{\vartheta}=1$ throughout $A$. These assertions hold for arbitrary real raw estimates, without a sign or accuracy hypothesis.* *The auxiliary score $I_{\vartheta}$ also has at most $K-1$ nonzero real entries and has an exposed row class with a bounded-support smooth witness equal to one on that class.
  - Explanation: Separated entry and rank thresholds expose bounded row classes with unit witnesses even for inaccurate signed raw arrays.
- **claim-paired-port-contract** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-atom-ports)): All main and preparatory row tables, auxiliary scores, and the smooth witnesses just constructed have bounded values and bounded row support. Every row access class used for a main or preparatory output, or for access to its auxiliary score, has bounded size and a smooth witness equal to one on every exposed entry, including exposed entries of weight zero. A witness itself is needed as an analytical row function, without an additional requirement to expose its support through a further witness. For a correction or its preparatory table let $A$ be its pre-incoming class from Equation <a href="#eq:atom-exposed-class" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:atom-exposed-class">[eq:atom-exposed-class]</a>. Retain an exposed entry $(x,y)\in A$ only when $$\#\{x':X_u(x')=1,\ (x',y)\in A\}\le K_c. \label{eq:atom-port-cap}$$ This deletion preserves all table values and gives at most $K-1$ outgoing and at most $K_c$ incoming exposed entries.* *These assertions hold separately for every computed version, provided that its values, ranks, scores, and access classes use the same final raw arrays and common task tuple. Access ports denote distinct entries: the implementation must expose each pair at most once and pair its incoming and outgoing ports consistently. Access to auxiliary scores alone has only the asserted row bound.
  - Explanation: Deleting every exposed precursor at an overfull column preserves values and supplies distinct bounded-degree paired relations.
- **claim-atom-assembly-comparison** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-atom-assembly)): Compare two versions with the same environment, rates, and task tuple. For a sparse normalized output write $H=P T g$ and $H'=P'T'g'$, where $P,P'$ are the pre-incoming clipped-ratio row functions (including their usage masks), $I,I'$ are their auxiliary scores, and $g,g'$ are their column multipliers. If $g,g'$ are the prescribed smooth cutoffs of bounded vertex arrays $U_i,U_i'$, then $$\mathfrak d_{u,f}(H,H')^s \le C\mathfrak d_{u,f}(P,P')^s +C\mathfrak d_{u,f}(I,I')^s +C\frac fu\sum_i\\|U_i-U_i'\\|_{f;s}^s. \label{eq:atom-assembly-bound}$$ For a sparse preparation omit the last term and use its unnormalized pre-incoming row function. The corresponding dense and detector row functions have no incoming or column-multiplier assembly cost.* *If $V_y,V_y'$ are the detector trials formed from $\mathcal S_i,\mathcal S_i'$ by their column order statistic, then $$\\|V-V'\\|_{f;s}^s \le C\mathfrak d_{f,f}(\mathcal S_i,\mathcal S_i')^s. \label{eq:atom-detector-comparison}$$
  - Explanation: Incoming caps control gate and column-multiplier errors by existing row and vertex metrics, without a full source-universe factor.
- **claim-affine-uniform-gap** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-env-affine)): Let $G_H=\mathrm{SL}_H(\mathbb Z)\ltimes\mathbb Z^H$, with fixed $H\ge3$. There is a fixed finite symmetric generating multiset and a lazy rational random walk on it whose action on every finite transitive $G_H$-set has a spectral gap bounded below by a positive constant depending only on $H$.
  - Explanation: A fixed lazy rational walk has a uniform spectral gap across finite transitive affine-group actions.
- **claim-conditional-mixing** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-env-gap)): Consider the fixed product of rank channels, conditioned on retention of one specified identifier per conditioned channel. Include any designated set of independent uniform bits, with length padded to a multiple of $H$, and freeze any remaining independent bits. There is a rational Markov averaging operator $K$ on this conditional space such that its stationary distribution is the indicated uniform conditional law and, for each fixed $2\le s<\infty$, $$\\|K^d-\Pi\\|_{L_s\to L_s}\le C_s2^{-c_sd} \qquad(d\ge0).$$ Here $\Pi$ is conditional expectation over the variables being averaged. The constants are independent of the field size, retention side lengths, bit lengths, indicated identifiers, and frozen bits.
  - Explanation: Conditional averaging mixes uniformly over retained-identifier slices and the designated free bits, independently of their finite sizes.
- **claim-validated-walk-variants** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-env-variants)): A length-$d$ word in the walk of Lemma <a href="#lem:env-gap" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:env-gap">20</a> can be expanded into a bounded-alphabet family of variants described by $O(d)$ bits such that:* 1. *each fixed variant acts bijectively and measure-preservingly on the full environment before any endpoint tests;* 2. *its transformation is independent of the indicated identifiers;* 3. *for each walk word and each environment in the required conditional slice, exactly one variant passes the slice and wrap tests at the indicated identifiers, and this variant gives the conditional walk transformation;* 4. *the sum of valid variants, each with the probability of its original walk word, is exactly the conditional average.* *The tests can be performed when their indicated vertices are visited. In the admissible implementation range, field elements and identifiers have $O(B)$ bits, the total auxiliary bit string has $O(B)$ bits, and $d=O(B)$. In that range the transformations and tests use $O(B)$ shared scratch space, and the retained description of a variant uses $O(d)$ bits.
  - Explanation: Identifier-independent bijective variants implement the conditional walk by delayed validation, retaining the original word weights.
- **claim-true-sample-means** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-est-true-means)): Using true stochastic tables in Equations <a href="#eq:est-direct" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:est-direct">[eq:est-direct]</a>–<a href="#eq:est-reward" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:est-reward">[eq:est-reward]</a> gives, after the indicated conditional averages, the prescribed raw inputs and vector values on their conditioning slices, with the stated zero extensions. In particular, the first row channel has target $d_y=G(x,y)/a$ and the second has target $\zeta q_y\mathbf1_{Y_t(y)}$.
  - Explanation: True atoms and the specified conditioning changes recover the raw matrix inputs, preparations, detector values and rewards.
- **claim-homogeneous-loss** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-est-loss)): The loss in Equation <a href="#eq:est-loss" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:est-loss">[eq:est-loss]</a> is comparable, by constants depending only on $s$, to $\|H^{1/s}-(H')^{1/s}\|^s$. It contracts under sums and nonnegative mixtures. If $H\le C_0G$ for a nonnegative $G$, then for every $a>0$ and $H'\ge0$, $$a\min\left\{1,\frac{\|H-H'\|}{a+G}\right\}^{s} \le C\mathcal L(H,H'), \label{eq:est-relative-loss}$$ where $C$ depends only on $s,C_0$.
  - Explanation: The homogeneous loss compares with root error, contracts under mixtures and bounds clipped relative error.
- **claim-scale-source-comparison** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-est-mean-comparison)): Compare a budget-$m$ sample term with the same term using true stochastic inputs. For a first-channel mean contribution use its clipped relative error against $1+d_y$. In the bound for its $s$th-power norm, the scale factor multiplying a child root-discrepancy power is, up to fixed constants, $$\begin{cases} b/a,&b\ge a,\\ (b/a)^{s-1},&b<a. \end{cases}$$ A child that releases the old source and restarts on a stage-rate $f$ domain costs in addition at most $f/u$ in norm power. Direct children retaining that source have no such factor. The same-scale vector and second-channel comparisons have constant scale cost, with $f/u$ only where a source is released. No independence of estimated factors is required.
  - Explanation: Scale changes and source release have explicit metric costs, established without independence assumptions on estimated factors.
- **claim-fine-bin-omission** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-est-omission)): If one fine bin is omitted, the norm of its normalized contribution is at most $C(b/a)^{(s-1)/s}$. This applies to direct terms, routed terms, and correction–bin products.
  - Explanation: Discarding a fine bin has a geometrically small normalized contribution, including inside correction products.
- **claim-immediate-path-descriptors** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-est-paths)): At a row group of slack $d$, immediate candidates have descriptions of $O(d)$ bits. With exact endpoint grouping their sums equal the specified conditional-walk increments. A product visits its midpoint by a paired correction move before using any factor at that midpoint. Its right-hand task tuple does not depend on the discarded old source. Every child estimator in such a candidate has budget at most $M-d$.
  - Explanation: Short immediate descriptors enumerate conditional-walk increments when grouped by actual endpoint; product children discard the old source.
- **claim-mean-prefix-error** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-est-mean-prefix)): Assume all earlier table and vector bounds with coefficient $C_b$. For an active task there is a fixed $B_1$, independent of the later choice of $A_*$, such that every mean prefix has norm at most $c_*2^{-p+B_1d_j}$ against its target. For the first channel the norm uses clipped relative discrepancy; for the second and for vectors it uses ordinary absolute discrepancy. The coefficient $c_*$ can be made arbitrarily small by increasing $A_*$.
  - Explanation: Telescoping child means and charging omitted bins gives a slack-dependent mean-prefix bound with an adjustable small coefficient.
- **claim-paired-raw-differences** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-est-raw-difference)): At a slack-$d$ group, the ordinary raw norm of an unaveraged paired difference is at most $$C C_b\,2^{-p-A_*+C_0d}, \label{eq:est-raw-bound}$$ where $C_0$ is fixed independently of the walk length coefficient. For two coupled versions of a budget-$r$ sample term, if the corresponding child discrepancies are bounded by $2^{-p'_r}\lambda_r$, their normalized raw difference is bounded by $2^{-p+C_0'd}\lambda_r$, summed over the finitely many child types. For a paired layer at budgets $m$ and $m-1$, apply this estimate to both parts. Its coupled discrepancy is consequently bounded by $2^{-p+C_0'd}(\lambda_m+\lambda_{m-1})$, after enlarging the fixed constant, or by the corresponding maximum over all children in the group. Every child in either part has budget at most $M-d$. For a fixed guessed measure-preserving variant and its valid endpoint restriction the same bounds hold. Counting all variants separately may increase $C_0'$ by a constant depending on the chosen walk length.
  - Explanation: Subtracting a common true-atom term bounds raw paired differences and coupled child discrepancies before spectral averaging.
- **claim-conditional-prefix-noise** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-est-prefix)): Assume exact local grouping, the earlier task error bounds, and that the sample functions depend only on variables varied by the conditional walk. Their uniform slice means are then deterministic at each indicated pair or vertex. Write $S_j^{\rm mean}$ for a mean prefix and $S_j^{\rm noise}=S_j-S_j^{\rm mean}$ for its noise. There are fixed $B_1$ and arbitrarily large prescribed $K_n$ such that $$\begin{aligned} \left\\|\min\left(1, \frac{\|S_j^{1,\rm mean}-d\|}{1+d}\right)\right\\|_{u,a;s} &\le c_*2^{-p+B_1d_j}, \label{eq:est-prefix-mean}\\ \\|S_j^{\rm noise}\\|_{u,a;s} &\le c_*2^{-p-K_nd_j}. \label{eq:est-prefix-noise} \end{aligned}$$ The second-channel mean uses its ordinary absolute norm, extended by zero off its usage domain, and satisfies the first bound. Vector means and noises satisfy the corresponding vertex bounds. The coefficient $c_*$ can be chosen as small as needed by task separation and walk constants.
  - Explanation: Exact grouping and complete averaging separate deterministic mean error from rapidly decaying conditional-walk noise.
- **claim-local-compression-update** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-buf-update)): The update has the following properties. It replaces every position of size at most $2u_0$ by the new default, is identity at every position of size at least $3u_0$, and lies coordinatewise between the input and the new default. The default is nondecreasing. The map from the input array and old default to the updated array and new default is uniformly Lipschitz in the sup norm. A list containing all exceptions can be chosen with at most $n_j$ positions, using only the previous list and the new candidates.
  - Explanation: The compression map replaces small positions by a monotone default, preserves large positions and keeps a bounded exception list.
- **claim-stationary-reference** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-buf-reference)): Let $L_{j-1}=T_{j-1}-S_{j-1}$ before the first overflow at $j$. Then $\\|L_{j-1}\\|_\infty\leq6\sum_{i<j}\rho_i$, and at every endpoint with $d_y\geq\eta$, $$\max_\nu\|L_{j-1}^\nu(y)\| \leq C\sum_{i<j}\rho_i e_i(y). \label{eq:buf-preloss}$$ Start a reference calculation at the input of group $j$ with the true array $(d,v)+L_{j-1}$, the same preceding default, and no further increments. Every subsequent compression preserves its relevant row outputs. Their root discrepancy from the true outputs is bounded by $C\sum_{i<j}\rho_i e_i$.
  - Explanation: Before overflow, preloss is small and chargeable to earlier errors; a stationary reference then preserves the relevant row outputs.
- **claim-post-overflow-stability** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-buf-relative-stability)): At a first overflow in group $j$, the discrepancy of final row-root outputs from the stationary reference of Lemma <a href="#lem:buf-reference" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:buf-reference">33</a> is at most $$C\sum_{i\geq j} C_1^{m_*-i+1}e_i. \label{eq:buf-relative-propagation}$$ The constant does not depend on the largest true first entry.
  - Explanation: After first overflow, output-root discrepancy is controlled by propagated prefix errors with no dependence on the largest true entry.
- **claim-heavy-count-rarity** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-buf-rarity)): At every specified endpoint, $$\mathbb P(\Theta_j\mid X_u(x)=Y_a(y)=1) \leq\frac{C}{n_j\rho_j}. \label{eq:buf-rarity}$$ The same bound holds with the narrower endpoint condition $Y_t(y)=1$. Moreover, for every prefix mean row supremum, $$\\|\mathbf1_{\Theta_j}\beta_i\\|_{L_s(\mu)} \leq Cc_*2^{-p+B_1d_i}(n_j\rho_j)^{-1/s}. \label{eq:buf-masked-mean}$$
  - Explanation: Conditional pair bounds make a true heavy count rare even at a forced endpoint, allowing deterministic mean errors to receive a rarity factor.
- **claim-integrated-compression-error** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-buf-error)): For fixed sufficiently large $c_1$, then $c_2$, and sufficiently rapid prefix-noise decay $K_n$, compression preserves the prescribed row error budget, with an arbitrarily small fixed coefficient when $c_*$ is chosen small. More precisely, $$\left(\int\sum_{H\in\mathcal H}\sum_y \|H(T_{m_*};y)^{1/s}-H(d,v;y)^{1/s}\|^s\,d\mu\right)^{1/s} \leq C_{\mathrm{buf}}c_*2^{-p}, \label{eq:buf-integrated}$$ where $C_{\mathrm{buf}}$ is fixed, independent of the number of groups, row width, and requested precision.
  - Explanation: Combining preloss, false overflow, true heavy counts and noise preserves the integrated row error budget uniformly over row width and group count.
- **claim-range-clamp-preservation** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-buf-clamping)): For fixed common increments satisfying Equation <a href="#eq:buf-clamp-margin" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:buf-clamp-margin">[eq:buf-clamp-margin]</a>, these clamps do not change the final relevant row functions. Each clamp is sup-norm nonexpansive, so in comparisons of two calculations it preserves the uniform Lipschitz propagation bound. The analogous assertion holds for vector sums clipped beyond their final sensitivity range and all remaining additive variation.
  - Explanation: Tail-separated clamps preserve final sensitive row functions for common increments and remain nonexpansive in coupled comparisons.
- **claim-exact-grouping-reserve** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-est-clean)): Suppose the earlier row and vector tasks have error bound $C_b2^{-p'}$ and the support and common-parameter properties of the atom section. Use exact comparisons locally, and vary every variable on which the sample terms depend. After compression and the range clamps above, all active row outputs, pre-incoming scores, and witnesses have error at most $(C_b/2)2^{-p}$. The same holds for the final clipped vectors and the assembled correction outputs, after choosing the fixed constants in the order specified below.
  - Explanation: Exact local comparisons and complete averaging leave spare error capacity after compression, clamping and atom assembly.
- **claim-short-fingerprint-family** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-fp-hash)): Suppose every endpoint has an injective, fixed-length binary encoding of length $L\le c_{\mathrm{ID}}B$. There is a uniform construction from $O(\log B)$ independent fair bits of a map $k:\{\text{endpoint IDs}\}\longrightarrow\{1,\ldots,B\}$ such that, for distinct fixed IDs $v,w$, $$\Pr[k(v)=k(w)]\le C/B\le C B^{-1/2}. \label{eq:fp-pair-collision}$$ Evaluating the map at a presented endpoint needs $O(\log B)$ arithmetic scratch in addition to access to its encoding.
  - Explanation: Polynomial evaluation followed by affine hashing constructs short endpoint keys with a fixed-pair collision bound and small arithmetic scratch.
- **claim-clean-salt-independence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-fp-clean)): Every clean value and structural choice for block $b$ is independent of that block’s effective salt and of later effective salts. In a task of budget $M\in\mathcal I_b$, the actual and clean row states immediately before the first group with $d\le2h_*$ are identical and independent of that salt. Their stored lists at this boundary have size $2^{O(h_*)}$. The deterministic slice-mean assertion required by Lemma <a href="#lem:est-prefix" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:est-prefix">31</a> holds for the clean calculation.
  - Explanation: Replacing same-block key tests by exact equality removes dependence on the current salt and verifies deterministic slice means.
- **claim-clean-envelope** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fp-envelope)): The set $\mathcal E_x$ is independent of the present salt and has size at most $2^{C_Eh_*}$ for a fixed $C_E$. All clean nondefault representatives in the small groups belong to this set. Consequently, conditional on the other data, $$\Pr[\text{two distinct IDs in $\mathcal E_x$ have the same key}] \le C\,2^{2C_Eh_*}B^{-1/2}. \label{eq:fp-envelope-collision}$$
  - Explanation: Clean witness supports determine a bounded salt-independent envelope containing the clean representatives, enabling a conditional collision union bound.
- **claim-escaped-candidate-charge** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fp-escape)): Suppose actual–clean child discrepancies at budget $m$ have their prescribed metric bounds $2^{-p_m}\lambda_m$. The contribution of $\mathcal F_x$ to any bounded final pre-incoming row output has norm at most $$2^{-p}\sum_{\substack{d\le2h_*\\m\in\mathcal I_b,\ m\le M-d}} 2^{C d}\lambda_m, \label{eq:fp-escape-charge}$$ where the sum includes the finitely many dependency types and their descriptor multiplicities in its constant $C$. Equivalently, one may use the maximum of $\lambda_m$ over the children of each slack group and increase $C$.
  - Explanation: An escaped actual candidate exposes a unit-versus-zero witness discrepancy; the actual left incoming cap controls right-child source release.
- **claim-increment-only-aliasing** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fp-buckets)): Consider one small group on $\mathcal F_x^c$. Let $\Delta_{\mathrm{ac}}(y),\Delta_{\mathrm{cl}}(y)$ be its unaliased increments, namely its true-ID sums using actual and clean children, respectively. Let $k_d\le2^{C d}$ bound its number of immediate descriptors, and let $\mathcal C_x$ denote a collision on $\mathcal E_x$. The discrepancy between the actual bucket-distributed increment and the clean true-ID increment is at most $$(k_d+1)\left( \sup_y\|\Delta_{\mathrm{ac}}(y)-\Delta_{\mathrm{cl}}(y)\| +\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_x}\sup_y\|\Delta_{\mathrm{cl}}(y)\| \right) \label{eq:fp-bucket-bound}$$ in sup norm, simultaneously for both channels. The old full-array discrepancy is added to this bound with coefficient one.
  - Explanation: Bucket collisions redistribute increments without merging old stored values, so the previous full-array discrepancy has no collision-height multiplier.
- **claim-direct-collision-error** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fp-direct)): The direct collision contribution to any final pre-incoming output has norm at most $$2^{-p}\,2^{C h_*}B^{-1/(2s)}, \label{eq:fp-direct-charge}$$ for a fixed $C$ independent of $D_1,D_2,\epsilon$ introduced below. All remaining contributions on $\mathcal F_x^c$ are bounded by actual–clean child discrepancy norms with an amplification at most $2^{C d}$ at slack $d$.
  - Explanation: Conditioning on salt-independent clean heights bounds the direct collision error while remaining perturbations are charged to children.
- **claim-uniform-block-coupling** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-fp-coupling)): The fixed constants can be chosen so that, for every task of budget $M\in\mathcal I_b$ and precision $p$, each prescribed actual–clean output discrepancy, including every pre-incoming score and witness, is at most $$2^{-p}\lambda_M,\qquad \lambda_M=2^{-D_1h_*+D_2(M-M_b)}. \label{eq:fp-lambda}$$ The same assertion holds for the ordinary vector metrics. Adding these discrepancies to the clean estimates proves the target error bounds for the actual tables and vectors.
  - Explanation: A budget induction absorbs child amplification and direct collisions, adding actual–clean discrepancy to the clean error reserve.
- **claim-actual-estimator-errors** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-fp-estimators)): For every allowed task, with precision $p$ defined in Equation <a href="#eq:est-precision" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:est-precision">[eq:est-precision]</a>, the actual row outputs, including the pre-incoming scores and support witnesses, satisfy $$\mathfrak d_{u,a}(\bar H,H)\le C_b2^{-p}.$$ The clipped vectors have the corresponding ordinary error bound. In particular, every allowed reward query satisfies $$\frac1N\mathbb E_\sigma\sum_{x\in V_l}\frac{X_u(x)}u \|\bar W_l(x)-W_l(x)\|^s\le C_b^s2^{-sp}. \label{eq:fp-reward-bound}$$ These estimates are uniform over the allowed task parameters and stage, and the constants are independent of the input and of $B$.
  - Explanation: Actual outputs, pre-incoming scores, witnesses and clipped vectors attain the prescribed uniform error metrics.
- **claim-restoring-catalytic-equality** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-fp-catalytic)): Let $V\in\{0,1\}^B$ be a shared vector with arbitrary initial contents. Suppose an excursion to either of two deterministically specified endpoints returns the cursor, and its path and result are independent of the incoming contents of $V$. Such excursions may use nested procedures which restore $V$. There is a procedure which xors the bit $\mathbf1_{k(v)=k(w)}$ into a local result bit, restores $V$, and needs only constant local data across four endpoint excursions.
  - Explanation: Repeated flips and reads compare endpoint keys while restoring arbitrary catalyst contents and avoiding suspended key indices.
- **claim-residue-exact-stream** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-arith-residue-stream)): Suppose $\|z\|\leq1$ and, for each $t\geq0$, a deterministic integer $N_t(z)$ satisfies $$\|N_t(z)-2^tz\|<2. \label{eq:arith-approximation}$$ Set $$z_0=N_0(z),\qquad z_t=N_t(z)-2N_{t-1}(z)\quad(t\geq1). \label{eq:arith-difference-digit}$$ Then $z_t\in\mathcal A$ and these digits represent $z$ exactly. For any fixed integer $q\geq4$, each output digit is determined by the required $N_t$ residues modulo $2^q$.
  - Explanation: Differences of deterministic integer approximations telescope to an exact redundant stream, with each digit recoverable from fixed residues.
- **claim-regenerated-gate-evaluation** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-arith-gate-evaluation)): Consider a finite Boolean circuit of bounded fan-in, with a specified output gate. Conditional gates may evaluate their selector first and then only their selected branch. Suppose the type and immediate predecessors of a gate, or its operand label and digit place if it is an input gate, can be computed from the root parameters and a path of child choices from the output gate. Suppose these computations use $O(B+t+d)$ scratch bits and make no operand or graph queries. Then depth-first evaluation retains $O(1)$ bits per gate on its current path, and requires no saved absolute gate address per gate. Its suspended record above an operand input has length at most a constant times the length of that path, plus any explicitly retained root-local record.
  - Explanation: A saved path of bounded gate choices suffices for depth-first evaluation because absolute gate addresses are regenerated in scratch.
- **claim-elementary-stream-operations** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-arith-elementary)): The normalized operations of taking a pair average, a maximum or minimum, and a fixed binary shift admit deterministic integers satisfying Equation <a href="#eq:arith-approximation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:arith-approximation">[eq:arith-approximation]</a>. Their residue procedures, for any fixed $q$, have the following properties. There are constants $C_0,C_1$ such that an operand place $j$ obeys $j\leq t+C_0$, its suspended local record has length at most $C_0+C_1(t-j)$, and the intrinsic local space is $O(t+1)$. Fixed finite compositions of these normalized operations have the same bounds, with enlarged constants. Fixed Boolean operations on returned digit codes, including sign decoding and conditional selection of code bits, add only constant local overhead.
  - Explanation: Finite comparisons, pair averages, extrema and fixed shifts have deterministic residue procedures with clock-decrement storage bounds.
- **claim-stream-multiplication** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-arith-multiplication)): For normalized exact input streams $x$ and $y$, multiplication has all the conclusions of Lemma <a href="#lem:arith-elementary" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:arith-elementary">50</a>. In particular, its suspended storage at an operand place $j$ is $O(1)+c(t-j)$, despite the potentially long product expansion.
  - Explanation: Minimum-index product bands make the operand-clock gap pay for suspended multiplication paths.
- **claim-positive-interval-reciprocal** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-arith-reciprocal)): Fix constants $0<a\leq b$. On inputs $x\in[a,b]$, a reciprocal, after a fixed known normalization, has the same operand-clock, suspended-record, and intrinsic-space bounds as in Lemma <a href="#lem:arith-elementary" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:arith-elementary">50</a>. Its local record may contain an $O(t+1)$-bit word only while querying input places $j\leq\lfloor t/2\rfloor+O(1)$.
  - Explanation: An early input prefix determines rational expansion coefficients; releasing that word before late suffix requests preserves suspended-space bounds.
- **claim-indexed-finite-ranks** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-arith-rank)): Fix $\kappa>0$ and $d\geq1$. Consider at most $2^{\kappa d}$ normalized values, indexed by descriptors of length at most $\kappa d$, and an order statistic specified by an $O(d)$-bit index. The semantic list length $n$ is public; the requested index is in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, or an out-of-range request returns a prescribed normalized constant. Absent descriptors may be assigned prescribed constant dummy values by structural validity predicates. This order statistic has deterministic integer approximations $N_t$ satisfying Equation <a href="#eq:arith-approximation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:arith-approximation">[eq:arith-approximation]</a>. Their residue procedures have constants $a,b,c$, depending only on the descriptor bounds, such that an operand digit query at $j$ obeys $$j\leq t+cd,\qquad L\leq ad+b(t-j), \label{eq:arith-local-bound}$$ where $L$ is the total suspended local record length. A structural validity query is assigned clock zero and has suspended length $O(d+t)$. The intrinsic local length is $O(d+t)$.
  - Explanation: Finite truncation comparisons and descriptor counting approximate the fixed semantic order statistic while handling invalid descriptors through defined dummies.
- **claim-bounded-sums-scales** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-arith-sums-scales)): Suppose an immediate descriptor domain has at most $2^{\kappa d}$ terms, all required binary scale exponents have magnitude at most $\kappa d$, and every intermediate output has a known range bound $2^{\kappa d}$. A sum over an empty domain is zero, and an average is taken over a public nonempty domain. Balanced sums or averages of these terms, followed by the required known rescalings and bounded clipping, satisfy Equation <a href="#eq:arith-local-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:arith-local-bound">[eq:arith-local-bound]</a> and have intrinsic local space $O(d+t)$.
  - Explanation: Balanced normalized reductions and known rescalings preserve the numerical interface, with explicit empty-sum and nonempty-average conventions.
- **claim-buffered-finite-tests** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-arith-buffered-test)): Let $d\geq1$, let $s$ and $u$ have known magnitude bound $2^{\kappa d}$, and suppose $u\geq\rho\geq2^{-\kappa d}$. There is a deterministic finite test that accepts every $s>2u$ and accepts only $s>u$. It uses $O(d)$-place digit queries after normalization, with intrinsic and suspended local lengths $O(d)$. Its result is independent of any subsequent numerical output clock.
  - Explanation: A fixed finite approximation distinguishes separated magnitude regimes without deciding equality of exact reals or following a later output clock.
- **claim-uniform-numerical-interface** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-thm-arith-interface)): Fix the digit alphabet, positive reciprocal intervals, and constants bounding the following recipe class. A recipe at slack $d\geq1$ has a fixed number of stages built from bounded arithmetic operations, fixed piecewise formulas using maxima, minima and clipping, the reciprocals of Lemma <a href="#lem:arith-reciprocal" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:arith-reciprocal">52</a>, indexed ranks as in Lemma <a href="#lem:arith-rank" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:arith-rank">53</a>, and sums and known scales as in Lemma <a href="#lem:arith-sums-scales" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:arith-sums-scales">54</a>. The stage and descriptor descriptions are generated from the root parameters by index computations using $O(B+d+t)$ scratch and no operand queries, and the total non-reduction dependency depth is bounded independently of $d$. Each indexed domain has size $2^{O(d)}$ and descriptors of length $O(d)$. Discrete domain and validity decisions are structural leaves or buffered tests with their own fixed precision conventions. Public coefficient leaves have exact normalized digit procedures using $O(B+d+t)$ shared scratch and making no operand or recursive graph queries.* *Then each normalized recipe value has a deterministic exact $\mathcal A$-stream. For its digit at clock $t$ there are uniform constants $a,b,c$ such that every requested operand digit $j$ satisfies $$j\leq t+cd,\qquad \text{total suspended local binary record length} \leq ad+b(t-j). \label{eq:arith-export}$$ An output code bit satisfies the same bounds. A structural leaf is requested at clock zero and has suspended local length at most $ad+bt$. The maximum intrinsic local record length is $O(d+t)$.* *All gate, digit and descriptor addresses can be regenerated from root parameters and the saved local records using $O(B+d+t)$ shared scratch and no recursive graph calls. When $d,t=O(B)$ this is $O(B)$ scratch. If a public rational coefficient has $O(B)$-bit numerator and denominator that can be generated in $O(B)$ scratch, its queried digits in this clock range also require only that shared $O(B)$ scratch.
  - Explanation: A syntactically bounded recipe class exports exact digit streams with regenerable addresses and telescoping suspended records.
- **claim-total-controller-realization** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-thm-ctrl-realization)): Fix the construction constants and an admissible top budget $M_{\mathrm{top}}=O(B)$. For every actual task tuple reachable from it, the row, vector and prefix interfaces defined in the preceding sections admit deterministic uniform implementations by restoring queries and cursor motions. The following assertions hold for every master environment, without an accuracy promise on its estimated values.* 1. *Every test or numerical digit query terminates, returns its defined value, and restores the cursor and catalyst. Its result is independent of incoming catalyst and scratch contents. Structural port and order choices are independent of a higher numerical request.* 2. *Terminal motions give the specified endpoints. Their excursions restore the cursor. Capped correction motions are partial paired maps with bounded inverse ports and safe behavior on invalid ports. Incoming score ranks compute the stipulated zero-padded ranks.* 3. *For a root numerical request at clock $t$, all records retained by the call and its descendants have total length $O(M_{\mathrm{top}}+t+1)$, and every descendant clock is $O(M_{\mathrm{top}}+t+1)$; the shared facilities use $O(B+M_{\mathrm{top}}+t+1)$ space. In particular an actual top request with $t=O(B)$ uses total deterministic $O(B)$ space.* *These implementations use no estimator oracle and retain no second vertex address across recursive graph operations.
  - Explanation: Restoring digit queries and cursor motions realize every reachable actual interface with total behavior and a simultaneous telescoping space bound.
- **claim-guarded-terminal-graph** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-ctrl-local-graph)): Suppose a fixed terminal recipe uses the preceding instruction types, has regenerable records, and obeys <a href="#eq:ctrl-local-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ctrl-local-bound">[eq:ctrl-local-bound]</a> on its designated executions. Suppose all its opaque transition queries are already implemented, are total on admissible arguments, and have the stated safe invalid-port behavior. Their returned bits, success flags, cursor outputs and port tokens are independent of incoming scratch and catalytic contents, and they restore the catalyst. Then there is a finite graph with outdegree at most one, uniformly associated with its root tuple, with these properties.* 1. *Its designated executions are precisely the prescribed terminal executions. Success states have no successor, and initiation and success tags are distinct.* 2. *Predecessor cases, ordered incidences, and paired edge movement are computable with a bounded number of case labels and one cursor. An opaque predecessor query is made only after its local bound has been checked.* 3. *If a transition query at $(w',j)$ is probed while the terminal root has parameters $(w,t)$, the complete live local portion of this probe, including a fixed number of edited or saved controller copies, has length $$\label{eq:ctrl-neighbor-bound} A(w-w')+D(t-j)$$ for fixed enlarged coefficients $A,D$. Shared facilities and the outside stack are not copied.* *The graph and all its guards are independent of an originating row, an outer stack’s data, and catalytic contents.
  - Explanation: Raw record certificates and total lower queries yield a finite deterministic guarded graph with safe predecessor probes and bounded local copies.
- **claim-inverse-tree-contour** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-ctrl-tour)): Let a finite deterministic graph of the form in Lemma <a href="#lem:ctrl-local-graph" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:ctrl-local-graph">61</a> have a specified canonical success halt. Its undirected component is a tree directed toward that halt. There are mutually inverse next-mark and previous-mark operations on its contour, where the marks are the root sentinel and one distinguished occurrence of each canonical initiation in the component. These operations require the current program state and bounded incidence control, but no saved root or contour-length counter.
  - Explanation: The success-halt component is a tree whose marked contour supports mutually inverse navigation without a saved root address.
- **claim-capped-incoming-motions** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-ctrl-cap)): Let a fixed row class have a constant port alphabet, distinct entries within each row, and a deterministic terminal program which maps its valid row ports to their endpoints. Assume the program is of the form in Lemma <a href="#lem:ctrl-local-graph" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:ctrl-local-graph">61</a>. For every fixed $K_c$ there are restoring tests and mutually inverse paired motions for precisely those class entries whose endpoint has at most $K_c$ incoming class entries. The inverse ports belong to $\{1,\ldots,K_c\}$. No additional endpoint address or unbalanced path is held across these operations.
  - Explanation: Bounded mark counting implements exactly the incoming-capped relation and supplies consistent inverse ports with restoring failure behavior.
- **claim-incoming-score-rank** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-ctrl-score-rank)): Let a constant-size forward row class cover every positive entry of a bounded nonnegative score table, with distinct entries in each row. Suppose pre-incoming score digits are restoring queries, and the class has a terminal program with the preceding interfaces. A fixed incoming $k$th-largest value, with zero padding, has exact redundant digits computed by a restoring procedure. Its local record above a place-$j$ score query at output approximation clock $t$ is $O(1+(t-j)_+)$, with a fixed overshoot $j\le t+c$, in addition to the structural allowance costs. A complete $O(t+1)$-bit score word is retained only over structural calls.
  - Explanation: Quantized-score success components permit incoming rank queries without keeping the final score word across late score-digit calls.
- **claim-ordered-terminal-excursions** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-ctrl-paths)): Every unbalanced path required by the estimator has the following ordered form: restoring selection and validity tests; local label maps and, if necessary, a paired left-factor motion; further restoring tests at that midpoint; at most one final terminal delegation; and then only local label completion. An excursion to its endpoint and back, for a pure local action, has regenerable records. It preserves the same allowance and clock bounds as this ordered path, up to fixed factors. No unbalanced spine is retained over a new high-cost query at its endpoint.
  - Explanation: Ordering restoring tests before final terminal delegation allows endpoint actions and rollback without suspending an unbalanced spine over another costly query.
- **claim-implemented-endpoint-comparison** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-ctrl-equality)): At slack $d$, comparisons of two valid candidate or old-list endpoints are restoring, catalyst-independent tests with $O(d)$ suspended structural control, in addition to the costs of their lower endpoint visits. They use no saved endpoint address. Their choice between an exact comparison and the designated fingerprint comparison is independent of a surrounding numerical clock.
  - Explanation: Exact or catalytic fingerprint comparison restores the cursor and catalyst without storing an endpoint address or changing with numerical precision.
- **claim-estimator-recipe-certificates** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-ctrl-recipes)): All actual estimator operations admit regenerable records and a fixed finite ordering of operation strata. At a prefix of slack $d$, each ordinary layer has $O(d)$ structural control, and a numerical path to an operand at clock $j$ has suspended record $$\label{eq:ctrl-recipe-bound} c_{\mathrm{str}}d+c_{\mathrm{num}}(t-j),\qquad j-t\le c_{\mathrm{dig}}d,$$ with fixed coefficients. Beyond the fixed strata of this prefix, a call is to the preceding prefix of slack $2d$, or to an estimator of budget at most $M-d$. The final row and incoming wrappers add a fixed number of strata at $d=1$. Every designated terminal execution obeys the corresponding boundary bounds before guards are imposed.
  - Explanation: A finite acyclic operation order certifies descriptor storage, numerical clock gaps and lower-budget dependencies before guards are imposed.
- **claim-effective-parameter-replay** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-ctrl-replay)): The records in Lemma <a href="#lem:ctrl-recipes" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:ctrl-recipes">67</a> are regenerable in the sense of Definition <a href="#def:ctrl-record" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:ctrl-record">59</a>. With respect to their own effective environments, actual procedures at a budget in block $b$ ignore all salt blocks later than $b$, including in structural orders, graph universes, guards and predecessor probes. Re-querying a table entry or using a paired port in either direction uses the same effective table tuple.
  - Explanation: Replaying active records reconstructs effective tuples and enforces salt visibility consistently for forward, inverse and synthetic-state queries.
- **claim-fixed-inverse-polynomial-accuracy** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-thm-fixed-precision)): Fix a randomized machine $\mathcal M$ with polynomial worst-case running time and $O(\log(n+2))$ work space, and fix an integer $d\ge1$. There is a uniform deterministic transducer that, on every input $x$ of length $n$, outputs a dyadic rational $z_x\in[0,1]$ with $$\|z_x-p_{\mathcal M}(x)\|\le(n+2)^{-d}.$$ Its work space and output length are $O(\log(n+2))$, and its running time is polynomial in $n+2$. The constants may depend on $\mathcal M$ and $d$, but not on the input.
  - Explanation: Conditional environment enumeration and a dyadic median yield deterministic fixed inverse-polynomial probability approximation with logarithmic live storage.
- **claim-specified-start-tail** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-final-majority)): Let $W\in[0,1]^V$, and suppose an estimator satisfies $$\frac1N\mathbb E\sum_{v\in V}\frac{X_f(v)}f \|\bar W(v)-W(v)\|^8\le C_b^8 2^{-8p}.$$ For any specified $z\in V$ and every $\eta>0$, $$\begin{aligned} \mathbb E\bigl[\|\bar W(z)-W(z)\|^8\mid X_f(z)=1\bigr] &\le N\frac f{\pi_f}C_b^8 2^{-8p}, \label{eq:final-conditional}\\ \Pr\bigl[\|\bar W(z)-W(z)\|>\eta\mid X_f(z)=1\bigr] &\le N\frac f{\pi_f}C_b^8 2^{-8p}\eta^{-8}. \label{eq:final-tail} \end{aligned}$$
  - Explanation: Selecting a start from the integrated moment bound incurs the stage-size factor; conditional Markov inequality gives the tail estimate.
- **claim-promise-logspace-equality** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cor-promise-bpl)): Under these conventions, $\mathsf{PromiseBPL}=\mathsf{PromiseL}$.
  - Explanation: The same approximation threshold gives a total deterministic separator, including halting outside the promise.
- **claim-certified-accepting-search** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-cor-certified-search)): Fix a randomized logarithmic-space machine $\mathcal M$ that halts within a fixed polynomial bound $T(n)\ge1$ on every input and every coin sequence, and fix an integer $c\ge0$. There is a uniform deterministic logarithmic-space, polynomial-time transducer that outputs an accepting computation of $\mathcal M$ whenever $$p_{\mathcal M}(x)\ge(n+2)^{-c}.$$ On every other input it outputs either an accepting computation or a failure symbol. If every accepting run of $\mathcal M$ emits a valid witness for a specified relation, the transducer can instead output such a witness with the same guarantee.
  - Explanation: Approximate continuation values guide an accepting run under the probability lower bound; a preliminary pass prevents emitting a rejecting run outside it.
- **claim-effective-simulation-compiler** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-thm-effective-simulation)): There is a terminating algorithm which, given a finite randomized machine description $M$ and positive integers $a,b$, emits a deterministic machine $D_M$ and positive integers $K,H,c$ with the following guarantee. If, on every input of length $n$ and every random tape, $M$ halts within $(n+2)^a$ steps, uses at most $b\lceil\log(n+2)\rceil$ work bits, and has acceptance probability at most $1/3$ on no inputs and at least $2/3$ on yes inputs, then $D_M$ decides the same language. On each input, that same execution uses at most $K\log(n+2)$ work bits and $H(n+2)^c$ elementary bit operations.
  - Explanation: A terminating syntactic compiler specializes a fixed deterministic separator and emits explicit resource bounds, conditional on supplied source guarantees.
- **claim-total-capped-interpreter** (algorithm, [source](#stmt-lem-compiler-interpreter)): There is one fixed randomized Turing machine $U$ with polynomial worst-case running time and $O(\log(m+2))$ counted work bits on every binary input of length $m$, with the following behavior. Set $$\label{eq:compiler-interpreter-cap} \lambda_m=\lceil\log_2(m+2)\rceil, \qquad R(m,d_{\mathrm{code}}) =\left\lfloor\frac{\lambda_m} {100(d_{\mathrm{code}}+1)^3}\right\rfloor.$$ On an input with prefix $$\label{eq:compiler-prefix} 1^{d_{\mathrm{code}}}0\,z\,1^n0\, E_{d_{\mathrm{code}}}(x),$$ it first requires $1\le d_{\mathrm{code}}\le\lambda_m$ and $R(m,d_{\mathrm{code}})\ge1$. It then simulates the encoded machine for at most $m$ transitions, allowing each counted work tape only coordinates in $[-R,R]$. It rejects malformed data, a requested move outside these bounds, or failure to halt by the end of the transition budget. Otherwise it returns the encoded machine’s decision. The suffix after the complete prefix has no parsing significance.
  - Explanation: A fixed interpreter validates actual finite code and enforces transition and tape-coordinate caps on every input before applying the source decision.

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-env-variants",
        "exact_quote": "A length-$d$ word in the walk of Lemma <a href=\"#lem:env-gap\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:env-gap\">20</a> can be expanded into a bounded-alphabet family of variants described by $O(d)$ bits such that:*\n\n1.  *each fixed variant acts bijectively and measure-preservingly on the full environment before any endpoint tests;*\n\n2.  *its transformation is independent of the indicated identifiers;*\n\n3.  *for each walk word and each environment in the required conditional slice, exactly one variant passes the slice and wrap tests at the indicated identifiers, and this variant gives the conditional walk transformation;*\n\n4.  *the sum of valid variants, each with the probability of its original walk word, is exactly the conditional average.*\n\n*The tests can be performed when their indicated vertices are visited. In the admissible implementation range, field elements and identifiers have $O(B)$ bits, the total auxiliary bit string has $O(B)$ bits, and $d=O(B)$.         "exact_quote": "At a slack-$d$ group, the ordinary raw norm of an unaveraged paired difference is at most $$C C_b\\,2^{-p-A_*+C_0d},\n \\label{eq:est-raw-bound}$$ where $C_0$ is fixed independently of the walk length coefficient.         "exact_quote": "Consider a finite Boolean circuit of bounded fan-in, with a specified output gate. Conditional gates may evaluate their selector first and then only their selected branch.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-arith-elementary",
        "exact_quote": "The normalized operations of taking a pair average, a maximum or minimum, and a fixed binary shift admit deterministic integers satisfying Equation <a href=\"#eq:arith-approximation\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:arith-approximation\">[eq:arith-approximation]</a>.         "anchor": "stmt-thm-arith-interface",
        "exact_quote": "Fix the digit alphabet, positive reciprocal intervals, and constants bounding the following recipe class. A recipe at slack $d\\geq1$ has a fixed number of stages built from bounded arithmetic operations, fixed piecewise formulas using maxima, minima and clipping, the reciprocals of Lemma <a href=\"#lem:arith-reciprocal\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:arith-reciprocal\">52</a>, indexed ranks as in Lemma <a href=\"#lem:arith-rank\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:arith-rank\">53</a>, and sums and known scales as in Lemma <a href=\"#lem:arith-sums-scales\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:arith-sums-scales\">54</a>. The stage and descriptor descriptions are generated from the root parameters by index computations using $O(B+d+t)$ scratch and no operand queries, and the total non-reduction dependency depth is bounded independently of $d$. Each indexed domain has size $2^{O(d)}$ and descriptors of length $O(d)$. Discrete domain and validity decisions are structural leaves or buffered tests with their own fixed precision conventions. Public coefficient leaves have exact normalized digit procedures using $O(B+d+t)$ shared scratch and making no operand or recursive graph queries.*\n\n\n*Then each normalized recipe value has a deterministic exact $\\mathcal A$-stream. A structural leaf is requested at clock zero and has suspended local length at most $ad+bt$. The maximum intrinsic local record length is $O(d+t)$.*\n\n*All gate, digit and descriptor addresses can be regenerated from root parameters and the saved local records using $O(B+d+t)$ shared scratch and no recursive graph calls. When $d,t=O(B)$ this is $O(B)$ scratch.         "anchor": "stmt-thm-ctrl-realization",
        "exact_quote": "Fix the construction constants and an admissible top budget $M_{\\mathrm{top}}=O(B)$. Structural port and order choices are independent of a higher numerical request.*\n\n2.  *Terminal motions give the specified endpoints. Their excursions restore the cursor. Capped correction motions are partial paired maps with bounded inverse ports and safe behavior on invalid ports. Incoming score ranks compute the stipulated zero-padded ranks.*\n\n3.  *For a root numerical request at clock $t$, all records retained by the call and its descendants have total length $O(M_{\\mathrm{top}}+t+1)$, and every descendant clock is $O(M_{\\mathrm{top}}+t+1)$; the shared facilities use $O(B+M_{\\mathrm{top}}+t+1)$ space.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-ctrl-local-graph",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose a fixed terminal recipe uses the preceding instruction types, has regenerable records, and obeys <a href=\"#eq:ctrl-local-bound\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:ctrl-local-bound\">[eq:ctrl-local-bound]</a> on its designated executions. Suppose all its opaque transition queries are already implemented, are total on admissible arguments, and have the stated safe invalid-port behavior. Their returned bits, success flags, cursor outputs and port tokens are independent of incoming scratch and catalytic contents, and they restore the catalyst. Then there is a finite graph with outdegree at most one, uniformly associated with its root tuple, with these properties.*\n\n1.  *Its designated executions are precisely the prescribed terminal executions. Success states have no successor, and initiation and success tags are distinct.*\n\n2.  *Predecessor cases, ordered incidences, and paired edge movement are computable with a bounded number of case labels and one cursor. An opaque predecessor query is made only after its local bound has been checked.*\n\n3.  *If a transition query at $(w',j)$ is probed while the terminal root has parameters $(w,t)$, the complete live local portion of this probe, including a fixed number of edited or saved controller copies, has length $$\\label{eq:ctrl-neighbor-bound}\n      A(w-w')+D(t-j)$$ for fixed enlarged coefficients $A,D$. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Strictly forward matrix** ([source](#sec:model)): A matrix indexed by a finite set $V$ is *strictly forward* if there is an integer time attached to every vertex and every nonzero entry goes to a strictly later time.
- **Substochastic matrix** ([source](#sec:model)): It is *substochastic* if its entries are nonnegative and each row sums to at most one.
- **Paired edge operation** ([source](#sec:model)): A *paired* edge operation returns the other endpoint together with its inverse port; applying the inverse operation restores the first endpoint.
- **Deterministic logarithmic space** ([source](#sec:intro)): The class $\mathsf L$ consists of languages decidable by deterministic machines in $O(\log(n+2))$ work space.
- **One-sided randomized logarithmic space** ([source](#sec:intro)): The class $\mathsf{RL}$ permits polynomial-time randomized machines in this space, with acceptance probability zero on no inputs and at least $1/2$ on yes inputs.
- **Two-sided randomized logarithmic space** ([source](#sec:intro)): For $\mathsf{BPL}$, the corresponding probabilities are at most $1/3$ and at least $2/3$.
- **Frame** ([source](#sec:env)): We call such an ordered collection of columns a *frame*.
- **Padded order statistic** ([source](#eq:hier-pilot-input)): For a finite multiset of nonnegative numbers, $\operatorname{rank}_j$ means its $j$-th largest member, with enough additional zeros that this is always defined.
- **Common default** ([source](#pm-h-24)): Call that common value the *default*.
- **Homogeneous loss** ([source](#eq:est-loss)): For nonnegative $H,H'$ define $$\mathcal L(H,H')= \begin{cases}\|H-H'\|^s/(H+H')^{s-1},&H+H'>0,\\0,&H=H'=0. \end{cases} \label{eq:est-loss}$$
- **Task precision** ([source](#eq:est-precision)): A task at integer budget $M\ge0$ has implicit precision $$p=\frac{M}{K_{\rm prec}}-\frac12\log_2\frac1a -\frac12\log_2\frac1u-A_*i_*.
- **Clean block calculation** ([source](#pm-h-44)): For an analytical comparison at a budget $M\in\mathcal I_b$, define the *clean calculation for block $b$* by replacing key comparisons by exact ID comparisons throughout that block, recursively in every child whose budget still belongs to $\mathcal I_b$.
- **Exact redundant digit stream** ([source](#pm-h-50)): An operand stream $(x_j)_{j\geq0}$ denotes the exact real number $$x=\sum_{j\geq0}x_j2^{-j},\qquad x_j\in\mathcal A.
- **Regenerable local record** ([source](#stmt-def-ctrl-record)): A local record is a delimited binary word with a tag from a fixed finite alphabet. It may contain immediate descriptor choices, bounded port or copy symbols, offsets, Boolean evaluation paths and pending bits, and the early numerical words permitted by Theorem <a href="#thm:arith-interface" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:arith-interface">56</a>. Head positions in such words are marked locally. A root tuple, a root operation and its numerical clock, together with the active records, determine every descendant tuple and clock by a scratch computation. This computation does not call a graph procedure and does not use a cursor that has been left behind. We call such records *regenerable*.
- **Raw allowance certificate** ([source](#stmt-def-ctrl-allowance)): A raw controller is the caller’s own selection, arithmetic, scoring or terminal-path record, excluding the working states of a query it calls. In a terminal program graph an explicit chain contains only its terminal-path controllers and, in a scoring program, its score suffix or completed score word. The interiors of cap traversals, inverse score ranks, numerical digit queries and paired motions are opaque queries; they are never explicitly pushed working graphs in this chain. A raw controller has an integer allowance $w\ge1$ and a numerical clock $t\ge0$. Fixed raw constants $a_0,b_0,a'>0$ give the following certificate at a call to a lower query or an explicitly pushed raw terminal controller at $(w',j)$: $$\label{eq:ctrl-local-bound} w'<w,\qquad j-t\le a'(w-w'),\qquad \ell\le a_0(w-w')+b_0(t-j).$$ Here $\ell$ counts only the suspended caller record, including its delimiters, return modes and pending data. It does not count the callee’s physical working space. Without a pending call its own raw records have length at most $a_0w+b_0t$. A structural operation has a canonical starting clock zero; numerical queries used by its finite-margin tests are included in this certificate.
- **Table tuple** ([source](#sec:ctrl-model)): A *table tuple* consists of the estimator type and stage, its statistical budget, scale and usage rates, channel roles and suffixes, and its effective environment.
- **Restoring test and quantity query** ([source](#sec:ctrl-model)): A *restoring test* returns one bit. A *quantity query* returns one bounded signed digit of a specified value. Both restore the cursor and the catalytic vector.
- **Range-valid argument** ([source](#pm-h-59)): An argument is *range-valid* when its tuple, operation type, cursor type, port code and clock lie in the permitted finite ranges.

| id | quantity | relation | value | regime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| q-probability-additive-error | Absolute acceptance-probability approximation error | ≤ | $2^{-q}$ | Constants depend only on the fixed machine. |
| q-probability-work-space | Work space for variable-precision probability approximation | = | $O(\log(n+2)+q)$ | The machine is fixed before reading the precision request. |
| q-probability-time | Time for variable-precision probability approximation | = | $(n+2)^{O(1)}2^{O(q)}$ | The constants are independent of the requested precision. |
| q-single-stage-size | Common stage vertex bound | = | $2^{C_NB}$ | The stage-size coefficient is fixed and may be enlarged. |
| q-factorial-correction-tail | Normalized fixed-point truncation error | ≤ | $e^{1/\theta_1}\frac{(L_Q/\theta_1)^k}{k!}$ | The iteration cutoff is uniform in the matrix, sampling rate, vertex set and multiplier. |
| q-copy-entry-density | Transition entry after a copy step | ≤ | $f/q$ | The copy radix and detector ranks are fixed in their prescribed order. |
| q-primary-reward-error | Acceptance probability minus primary-copy reward | ≤ | $\|V_0\|\,2^{-(H-1)l}$ | The stage number varies; hierarchy constants are fixed. |
| q-correction-normalizer-lower-bound | Conditional joint gate mean on positive correction support | ≥ | $3/4$ | No corresponding positive lower bound is required at a zero multiplier. |
| q-conditional-walk-contraction | Conditional averaging operator discrepancy | ≤ | $C_s2^{-c_sd}$ | Constants are uniform in field size, retention sides, bit lengths, identifiers and frozen bits. |
| q-fine-omission-error | Norm of an omitted normalized fine-bin contribution | ≤ | $C(b/a)^{(s-1)/s}$ | The constant does not depend on the omitted fine scale. |
| q-short-key-collision | Collision probability for distinct fixed endpoint identifiers | ≤ | $C/B$ | This is a fixed-pair guarantee; adaptive candidates require the block comparison. |
| q-reward-moment-error | Integrated reward discrepancy power | ≤ | $C_b^s2^{-sp}$ | Constants are independent of input and stage-size parameter. |
| q-stream-tail | Absolute error of a redundant-stream truncation | ≤ | $6\,2^{-K}$ | The truncation place varies over nonnegative integer clocks. |
| q-integer-approximation-error | Scaled error of a deterministic integer approximation | < | $2$ | Each clock uses its own deterministic approximation convention. |
| q-arithmetic-suspended-storage | Suspended numerical record length at an operand query | ≤ | $ad+b(t-j)$ | Uniform coefficients depend on the fixed recipe class. |
| q-controller-simultaneous-storage | Total retained controller and descendant records | = | $O(M_{\mathrm{top}}+t+1)$ | Root clock and admissible top budget determine descendant storage and clock bounds. |
| q-fixed-accuracy | Fixed inverse-polynomial approximation error | ≤ | $(n+2)^{-d}$ | Constants may depend on the machine and fixed accuracy exponent. |
| q-conditioned-start-tail | Conditional specified-start error-tail probability | ≤ | $N\frac f{\pi_f}C_b^8 2^{-8p}\eta^{-8}$ | The stage-size factor must be paid by statistical precision. |
| q-compiled-work-bits | Work bits of the emitted deterministic machine | ≤ | $K\log(n+2)$ | The emitted coefficient depends on finite source and library syntax. |
| q-compiled-bit-time | Elementary bit operations of the emitted deterministic machine | ≤ | $H(n+2)^c$ | The compiler emits the source-specific coefficient and exponent. |
