<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-configurations** [claim](#stmt-lem-model-reduction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-model-reduction): Time-layer configurations, enumerate distinct paired ports and collect reward only at final time. -> A finite strictly forward substochastic transition model for acceptance probability.
- **step-rank-channels** [claim](#stmt-lem-env-ranks) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-env-ranks): Condition uniform coefficient matrices on frame success and use evaluation ranks and affine changes of variables. -> Marginal, conditional-pair, lower-tail and affine-invariance estimates.
- **step-fixed-correction** [claim](#stmt-lem-hier-fixed-point) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-hier-fixed-point): Solve each forward row in column order and count ordered substitutions within that row's support. -> A comparison fixed point and a universe-independent finite truncation count.
- **step-pilot-monotonicity** [claim](#stmt-lem-hier-pilot-bounds) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-hier-pilot-bounds): Induct on pilot and actual iterations using monotonicity and nonnegative matrix products. -> Uniform row and entry bounds and actual-to-pilot domination.
- **step-detector-columns** [claim](#stmt-lem-hier-column-test) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-hier-column-test): Combine row-gate Markov bounds with retained-start lower tails, without assuming independent row failures. -> A bounded substantial-entry count in every correction-enabled column.
- **step-finite-residual** [claim](#stmt-lem-hier-residual) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-hier-residual): Use the finite subsolution residual for positivity and domination, and the comparison fixed point for good-column density. -> A forward substochastic residual dominating its unsigned terms.
- **step-copy-routing** [claim](#stmt-prop-hier-copy-step) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-hier-copy-step): Route residual entries among destination copies and count detector incidences to bound active extra copies. -> Density reduction, bounded active growth and weighted intertwining.
- **step-reward-hierarchy** [claim](#stmt-prop-hier-reward-target) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-hier-reward-target): Induct the cumulative algebraic identity and bound residual row mass along primary copies. -> A shallow bounded reward target approximating every base probability.
- **step-dense-atoms** [claim](#stmt-lem-atom-dense) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-atom-dense): Split entries by scale and divide gated contributions by their exact preparatory conditional mean. -> Bounded-support dense and routed atoms with exact bin means.
- **step-bin-products** [claim](#stmt-lem-hier-bin-products) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-hier-bin-products): Multiply bounded deterministic bin rows by a nonnegative finite correction. -> Uniform fine-product row mass and entry bounds.
- **step-correction-atoms** [claim](#stmt-lem-atom-correction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-atom-correction): Bound row and incoming gate failures and normalize on positive multiplier support; handle zero multipliers separately. -> Exact correction means with bounded clipped denominators.
- **step-exposed-margins** [claim](#stmt-lem-atom-margins) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-atom-margins): Separate entry thresholds from full-array rank thresholds and use finite-accuracy tests inside the margins. -> Bounded exposed classes and unit smooth witnesses for arbitrary raw arrays.
- **step-port-degrees** [claim](#stmt-lem-atom-ports) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-atom-ports): Remove all precursor ports at overfull columns, whose incoming gate already vanishes. -> Distinct bounded outgoing and incoming correction relations.
- **step-assembly-errors** [claim](#stmt-lem-atom-assembly) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-atom-assembly): Split product-root discrepancies and sum column effects using incoming caps and common task tuples. -> Assembly and detector-trial discrepancy estimates.
- **step-affine-gap** [claim](#stmt-lem-env-affine) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-env-affine): Project toward translation invariants using relative property and then toward full invariants using the linear-group gap. -> A fixed rational lazy walk with a uniform finite-action spectral gap.
- **step-conditional-mixing** [claim](#stmt-lem-env-gap) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-env-gap): Express retained channels as frame and box coordinates, form a product action and interpolate the spectral estimate. -> Uniform conditional averaging contraction.
- **step-walk-variants** [claim](#stmt-lem-env-variants) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-env-variants): Enumerate bounded wrap choices as full-environment bijections and validate a unique wrap at each visited identifier. -> Short identifier-independent variants with exact original-word weights.
- **step-true-means** [claim](#stmt-lem-est-true-means) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-est-true-means): Change nested retention slices before averaging and apply the true left and right atom normalizations. -> Correct raw, preparatory, detector and reward mean targets.
- **step-homogeneous-loss** [claim](#stmt-lem-est-loss) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-est-loss): Factor differences of powers and apply mixture contraction to the homogeneous loss. -> A bridge between root discrepancies and clipped relative errors.
- **step-scale-domain-costs** [claim](#stmt-lem-est-mean-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-est-mean-comparison): Apply mixture contraction at coarse scales, change fine conditioning before taking powers and eliminate old sources with incoming caps. -> Scale and source-release costs without independence of estimated errors.
- **step-fine-omissions** [claim](#stmt-lem-est-omission) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-est-omission): Combine fine entry bounds with bounded deterministic row mass. -> Geometrically decaying omitted-bin error.
- **step-immediate-paths** [claim](#stmt-lem-est-paths) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-est-paths): Enumerate bounded descriptors and validate variants, grouping actual endpoints before forming paired differences. -> Exact conditional-walk increments and strictly lower-budget children.
- **step-prefix-means** [claim](#stmt-lem-est-mean-prefix) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-est-mean-prefix): Telescope available scale means to their exact last budgets and charge wholly omitted fine scales separately. -> Small-coefficient deterministic mean-prefix bounds.
- **step-raw-paired-bounds** [claim](#stmt-lem-est-raw-difference) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-est-raw-difference): Subtract the same true sample term from both budgets and apply bounded-factor, row and incoming comparisons. -> Crude raw and coupled discrepancy bounds for fixed variants.
- **step-prefix-noise** [claim](#stmt-lem-est-prefix) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-est-prefix): Apply the conditional operator estimate to each whole paired endpoint function, then sum slack groups. -> Separate deterministic mean and rapidly decaying noise bounds.
- **step-compression-map** [claim](#stmt-lem-buf-update) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-buf-update): Use rank-based thresholds and bounded displacement clipping to form a new default and retain exceptions. -> A uniformly Lipschitz bounded-list update.
- **step-stationary-reference** [claim](#stmt-lem-buf-reference) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-buf-reference): Charge small pre-overflow changes at sensitive targets and preserve row functions in a no-further-increment reference. -> A stationary reference and controlled preloss.
- **step-overflow-stability** [claim](#stmt-lem-buf-relative-stability) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-buf-relative-stability): Separate gate-closed rows from rows with few large entries and use saturated sentinels to remove large absolute errors. -> Post-overflow root stability independent of the largest true entry.
- **step-heavy-rarity** [claim](#stmt-lem-buf-rarity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-buf-rarity): Bound the deterministic heavy set by mass and use conditional pair retention before integrating deterministic mean-error magnitudes. -> Conditional heavy-count rarity and masked mean-error bounds.
- **step-compression-error** [claim](#stmt-prop-buf-error) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-buf-error): Integrate disjoint first-overflow cases, charging false overflows to endpoint error and true heavy counts to conditional rarity. -> A uniform integrated compression error reserve.
- **step-range-clamps** [claim](#stmt-lem-buf-clamping) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-buf-clamping): Maintain matching saturated behavior outside all sensitivity ranges using a common tail margin. -> Bounded numerical ranges preserving final row functions and nonexpansive coupling.
- **step-clean-reserve** [claim](#stmt-prop-est-clean) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-est-clean): Apply compression to deterministic means and noise, preserve outputs under common clamps and then assemble incoming and column factors. -> An active-task bound with spare coefficient.
- **step-short-fingerprints** [claim](#stmt-lem-fp-hash) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-fp-hash): Evaluate binary identifier polynomials over a prime field and apply affine residue bucketing from raw fair bits. -> Short keys with fixed-pair collision and scratch bounds.
- **step-clean-independence** [claim](#stmt-lem-fp-clean) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-fp-clean): Induct on budget and structural operation order, replacing every same-block key test by exact equality. -> Salt-independent clean structure and deterministic clean slice means.
- **step-witness-envelope** [claim](#stmt-lem-fp-envelope) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-fp-envelope): Unite boundary representatives and clean witness supports over all small-group descriptors. -> A salt-independent candidate envelope and conditional collision bound.
- **step-escape-charge** [claim](#stmt-lem-fp-escape) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-fp-escape): Locate an offending unit witness and eliminate old starts with the actual exposed correction incoming cap. -> Escaped-candidate error charged to lower-budget witness discrepancies.
- **step-bucket-algebra** [claim](#stmt-lem-fp-buckets) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-fp-buckets): Compare distributed bucket increments with unaliased actual and clean sums while keeping old values at their original identifiers. -> A full-array perturbation bound without old-value collision charges.
- **step-collision-charge** [claim](#stmt-lem-fp-direct) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-fp-direct): Propagate clean increment heights and condition on their salt-independent sigma-field before applying the envelope collision estimate. -> A direct collision term plus amplified child discrepancies.
- **step-coupled-induction** [claim](#stmt-prop-fp-coupling) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-fp-coupling): Induct strongly on budget and choose block gains after crude propagation constants to absorb collision and child charges. -> Uniform actual–clean coupling and actual target bounds.
- **step-actual-estimators** [claim](#stmt-thm-fp-estimators) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-fp-estimators): Add coupled discrepancies to the clean spare bound and include inactive bounded-output cases. -> Actual row, witness, score and reward moment bounds.
- **step-catalytic-equality** [claim](#stmt-lem-fp-catalytic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-fp-catalytic): Alternate endpoint-local flips and reads so incoming catalyst contents cancel and are restored. -> Key equality with bounded suspended local data.
- **step-residue-streams** [claim](#stmt-lem-arith-residue-stream) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-arith-residue-stream): Take differences of successive scaled integer approximations and decode bounded signed residues. -> Exact redundant digit streams.
- **step-gate-regeneration** [claim](#stmt-lem-arith-gate-evaluation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-arith-gate-evaluation): Save bounded child choices and pending bits while regenerating gate descriptions from the root path. -> Depth-first evaluation without saved absolute gate addresses.
- **step-elementary-arithmetic** [claim](#stmt-lem-arith-elementary) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-arith-elementary): Compare finite truncations with an absorbing finite-state sign process and compute only needed low residues. -> Elementary normalized operations with clock-gap storage bounds.
- **step-multiplication-bands** [claim](#stmt-lem-arith-multiplication) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-arith-multiplication): Partition products by minimum input index and combine signed floor-shifted band residues. -> Multiplication with bounded overshoot and suspended records.
- **step-reciprocal-prefix** [claim](#stmt-lem-arith-reciprocal) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-arith-reciprocal): Build an early prefix for rational linear-expansion coefficients and release it before late suffix requests. -> Normalized reciprocal queries satisfying the early-word lifetime rule.
- **step-indexed-ranks** [claim](#stmt-lem-arith-rank) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-arith-rank): Order finite truncations with descriptor tie-breaking, count preceding entries and select residue bits. -> Fixed semantic order-statistic streams with structural-leaf bounds.
- **step-sums-scales** [claim](#stmt-lem-arith-sums-scales) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-arith-sums-scales): Normalize terms, reduce by balanced pair averages and restore known scales with bounded clipping. -> Sum and average recipes with telescoping numerical records.
- **step-buffered-tests** [claim](#stmt-lem-arith-buffered-test) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-arith-buffered-test): Compare finite approximations inside a fixed relative gap using precision determined by structural parameters. -> Clock-independent structural decisions within prescribed margins.
- **step-numerical-interface** [claim](#stmt-thm-arith-interface) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-arith-interface): Compose a bounded recipe family with common clock coefficients and regenerate every gate and digit address. -> Exact digit interfaces with certified suspended and intrinsic storage.
- **step-local-program-graphs** [claim](#stmt-lem-ctrl-local-graph) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ctrl-local-graph): Guard raw terminal records and enumerate bounded inverse instruction cases, treating lower queries as opaque transitions. -> Finite deterministic graphs with safe bounded-copy predecessor probes.
- **step-contour-navigation** [claim](#stmt-lem-ctrl-tour) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ctrl-tour): Use incidence rotation and edge flip around the success-root tree with a sentinel mark. -> Mutually inverse next-mark and previous-mark operations.
- **step-incoming-pairing** [claim](#stmt-lem-ctrl-cap) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ctrl-cap): Count marked initiations up to the fixed cap and restore failed searches by inverse mark jumps. -> Capped paired motions with bounded inverse ports.
- **step-incoming-ranks** [claim](#stmt-lem-ctrl-score-rank) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ctrl-score-rank): Assemble score suffixes from late to early digits and tour success components by quantized score level. -> Restoring incoming ranks with no full score word across late digit calls.
- **step-ordered-excursions** [claim](#stmt-lem-ctrl-paths) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ctrl-paths): Order tests, paired midpoint motion and final terminal delegation, then undo the retained visiting spine after a pure endpoint action. -> Restoring excursions without a saved endpoint address.
- **step-endpoint-comparison** [claim](#stmt-lem-ctrl-equality) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ctrl-equality): Use exact identifier scans at large slack and restoring catalytic key comparisons at small slack. -> Restoring structural comparisons independent of output precision.
- **step-concrete-certificates** [claim](#stmt-lem-ctrl-recipes) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ctrl-recipes): Certify immediate paths, bucket flags, compression ranks, fresh presence wrappers and final incoming operations in a finite dependency order. -> Raw recipe and clock certificates before guard insertion.
- **step-parameter-replay** [claim](#stmt-lem-ctrl-replay) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ctrl-replay): Scan active records to regenerate stages, rates, suffixes, effective environments, operation clocks and permitted salt coordinates. -> Common effective tuples and salt visibility for every query direction.
- **step-controller-space** [claim](#stmt-thm-ctrl-realization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rem-ctrl-effective-environment): Assign decreasing runtime allowances, construct lower procedures well-foundedly and telescope physical record potentials along the stack. -> Total uniform actual interfaces with simultaneous logarithmic storage.
- **step-start-conditioning** [claim](#stmt-lem-final-majority) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-final-majority): Keep the specified nonnegative summand and apply conditional Markov inequality. -> Specified-start conditional moment and tail bounds.
- **step-fixed-precision-median** [claim](#stmt-thm-fixed-precision) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-final-majority-2): Choose hierarchy and statistical precision, truncate total digit queries and repeatedly enumerate original conditional encodings to select a median. -> Uniform fixed inverse-polynomial approximation with counted outer registers and polynomial time.
- **step-class-equality** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-final-majority-3): Threshold a fixed-accuracy answer and combine deterministic inclusion with independent repetition for one-sided error. -> The asserted equality of deterministic and bounded-error randomized logarithmic space.
- **step-promise-separation** [claim](#stmt-cor-promise-bpl) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-promise-bpl): Use the same approximation threshold and retain totality outside the promise. -> A total deterministic logarithmic-space separator.
- **step-unary-precision-padding** [claim](#stmt-thm-probability) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-promise-bpl-2): Simulate a fixed exponent approximator on an implicit padded input and round its captured dyadic output exactly. -> A single variable-precision algorithm with the stated space and time bounds.
- **step-certified-search** [claim](#stmt-cor-certified-search) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-certified-search): Choose successors by approximate continuation values, check the terminal result and repeat deterministic choices to stream only a certified accepting run. -> An accepting computation or valid emitted witness under the promise; otherwise an accepting computation or failure.
- **step-capped-interpreter** [claim](#stmt-lem-compiler-interpreter) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-compiler-interpreter): Validate finite code before allocation and enforce bounded tape strips and a transition clock on every input. -> A total randomized interpreter with unconditional resource caps.
- **step-effective-compiler** [claim](#stmt-thm-effective-simulation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-auto-remark-1): Fix a deterministic separator for the capped interpreter, specialize virtual-input callbacks and compute simultaneous bounds from emitted finite syntax. -> A terminating compiler emitting a deterministic machine and explicit work-bit and bit-time bounds.

```json
          "exact_quote": "For every fixed column multiplier $0\\leq g\\leq1$, there is a unique strictly forward nonnegative solution of $$E_*(x,y)=fQ((C+E_*C)(x,y)/f)g(y).\n \\label{eq:hier-fixed-point}$$ For the recurrence in Equation <a href=\"#eq:hier-fixed-g-iteration\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:hier-fixed-g-iteration\">[eq:hier-fixed-g-iteration]</a>, $0\\leq E_i\\leq E_*$, and for every $k\\geq0$, $$\\max_{x,y}\\frac{E_*(x,y)-E_k(x,y)}f\n \\leq\n e^{1/\\theta_1}\\frac{(L_Q/\\theta_1)^k}{k!}.\n \\label{eq:hier-factorial}$$ In particular $k_*$ can be chosen as a fixed integer so that the right side of Equation <a href=\"#eq:hier-factorial\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:hier-factorial\">[eq:hier-factorial]</a> at $k=k_*$ is at most $q^{-1}/32$, uniformly in $C,f,V$, and $g$.",
```

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **inv-catalyst-restoration**: The equality procedure restores every bit of the shared vector to its incoming value.
- **inv-key-equality-xor**: The result bit is toggled exactly when the presented endpoint keys agree, independently of incoming vector contents.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-catalyst-dependent-paths**: Let endpoint selection depend on catalytic contents while performing the restoring equality test. -> An intervening flip may change the selected endpoint, so repeated visits no longer cancel.
- **anti-key-equality-as-id-equality**: Treat a successful fingerprint comparison as an exact endpoint identity certificate. -> Distinct fixed identifiers may have matching keys; restoration does not eliminate fingerprint collisions.
- **anti-local-test-as-global-space-proof**: Use a finite catalytic identity check to certify the complete deterministic simulation and its simultaneous space bound. -> The check does not construct endpoint excursions, validate recursive record lifetimes, or account for shared facilities and suspended callers.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `constructive`. The restoring equality lemma gives a finite constructive identity: catalytic flips and reads toggle the result by key equality and restore arbitrary incoming vector contents. This harness checks that local identity exhaustively on bounded vector widths. It does not certify endpoint excursion implementations, recursive storage bounds, fingerprint probabilities, or the main derandomization theorem.

```python
# INPUTS: JSON object containing integer width.
# PRECONDITIONS: Accepted widths are integers from 1 through 6; booleans are excluded.
# OUTPUTS: For every initial vector, ordered key pair, and result bit, emit [result, final_vector_mask].
# TIME: O(2**width * width**3) elementary bit and list operations.
# SPACE: O(width) working storage excluding the streamed output.
# ARITHMETIC: Exact Python integers, binary list entries, and xor.
# FAILURE: Malformed or out-of-domain input emits a fixed error object.
import itertools
import json
import sys

def equality(vector, left, right, result):
    # First endpoint excursion.
    vector[left] ^= 1
    # Second endpoint excursion.
    result ^= vector[right]
    # Third endpoint excursion.
    vector[left] ^= 1
    # Fourth endpoint excursion.
    result ^= vector[right]
    return result

def main():
    try:
        request = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        print('{"error":"invalid width"}')
        return
    width = request.get('width') if type(request) is dict else None
    if type(width) is not int or not 1 <= width <= 6:
        print('{"error":"invalid width"}')
        return
    first = True
    sys.stdout.write('[')
    for bits in itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=width):
        for left in range(width):
            for right in range(width):
                for initial_result in (0, 1):
                    vector = list(bits)
                    result = equality(vector, left, right, initial_result)
                    final_mask = 0
                    for bit in vector:
                        final_mask = 2 * final_mask + bit
                    if not first:
                        sys.stdout.write(',')
                    first = False
                    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([result, final_mask], separators=(',', ':')))
    sys.stdout.write(']\n')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## 5. Domain engineering contracts

| domain | applies | strength | maturity | basis | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| software | True | strong | adaptable | inferred | The effective compiler constructs a deterministic decision machine from a randomized source description and supplied resource bounds. Correctness depends on the source satisfying those bounds and its bounded-error promise. |

## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-worst-case-source-resources** (hypothesis): Probability approximation requires a fixed randomized machine with polynomial worst-case running time and logarithmic work space. An expected running-time bound alone does not supply this hypothesis. Blocked use: ['Apply the approximation theorem to a machine whose running time is bounded only in expectation.', 'Apply the simulation without establishing the stated counted work-space bound.']
- **limit-count-all-live-storage** (formal_scope): The space convention includes traversed writable cells and all simultaneously live counters, numerical registers and suspended calls. Blocked use: ['Exclude blank visited cells from the space charge.', 'Count each recursive routine separately while omitting its suspended callers.']
- **limit-unary-precision-time** (approximation): The precision request is unary, and general requested precision retains an exponential running-time dependence. Blocked use: ['Claim polynomial running time in an unrestricted precision request.', 'Replace the unary precision interface by a binary interface while retaining the stated resource guarantee.']
- **limit-fixed-accuracy-constants** (hypothesis): The inverse-polynomial approximation theorem fixes the accuracy exponent together with the source machine; its constants need not be uniform over changing exponents. Blocked use: ['Treat a varying accuracy exponent as an ordinary input to the fixed-accuracy transducer.']
- **limit-forward-transition-model** (formal_scope): The finite inverse construction uses time labels that make every nonzero transition strictly forward. It is not an unrestricted inverse construction for cyclic substochastic matrices. Blocked use: ['Use the finite inverse expression unchanged for a cyclic transition matrix.', 'Infer an unrestricted directed-reachability algorithm from the configuration reduction.']
- **limit-admissible-retention-range** (hypothesis): Rank-channel guarantees require the prescribed rate grid, distinct identifiers where the conditional pair bound is used, and a sufficiently large prime field. Blocked use: ['Apply the conditional pair estimate to coincident identifiers.', 'Request retention scales outside the admissible field range.']
- **limit-fixed-point-is-comparison** (formal_scope): The correction fixed point is an analytical comparison object; the hierarchy uses the prescribed finite iteration with its column multiplier held fixed. Blocked use: ['Require evaluation or storage of the full fixed point as an algorithm stage.', 'Change the column multiplier during the actual fixed-multiplier recurrence and retain its truncation guarantee.']
- **limit-true-atom-unbiasedness** (approximation): Exact conditional-mean identities concern true stochastic tables. Applying the formulas to approximate raw signals does not itself preserve unbiased normalization. Blocked use: ['Declare estimated normalized atoms unbiased merely because true atoms have exact means.', 'Assume estimated factors are independent when they share the environment.']
- **limit-normalization-slice** (hypothesis): The broad preparatory domain and narrower usage-conditioning slice are separate parts of the normalized-table interface. Blocked use: ['Reuse a preparatory denominator after changing its usage-conditioning slice.', 'Discard the usage membership mask during normalized assembly.']
- **limit-port-support-versus-access** (formal_scope): Bounded analytical support does not alone provide a single-address enumeration and paired-port implementation. Exposed entries must be distinct, including exposed entries of weight zero. Blocked use: ['Count multiple discovery paths as separate ports for the same entry.', 'Infer paired random access solely from a degree bound.']
- **limit-common-task-tuple** (hypothesis): Assembly comparisons require the same environment, rates and common task tuple. A right factor reached through a correction cannot retain the discarded old source as an extra parameter. Blocked use: ["Change an entry's meaning according to the path that discovered it.", 'Sum right-child errors over old sources while using source-dependent right-child tuples.']
- **limit-complete-conditional-averaging** (hypothesis): The deterministic slice-mean argument requires exact local grouping and averaging over every variable used by the sample function. Blocked use: ['Freeze an environment coordinate that still affects a sample term and then treat the slice mean as deterministic.', 'Measure paired budget differences before combining contributions at the same actual endpoint.']
- **limit-common-increments-for-clamp-equality** (hypothesis): Equality of final row functions under range clamping requires fixed common increments with the stated tail margin. Coupled calculations with different increments receive a nonexpansive comparison, not an equality guarantee. Blocked use: ['Assert that clamped and unclamped adaptive calculations select identical lists or ports.', 'Apply the clamp-preservation equality to independently changing bucket increments.']
- **limit-adaptive-fingerprint-scope** (formal_scope): A fixed-pair collision estimate does not by itself control adaptively chosen endpoints; the clean-block comparison and salt visibility rule are necessary parts of the analysis. Blocked use: ['Treat matching endpoint keys as proof of exact identifier equality.', 'Apply the fixed-pair probability bound directly to salt-dependent candidate sets.']
- **limit-increment-only-buckets** (hypothesis): Fingerprint buckets combine new increments while retaining old representatives and their stored values separately. Blocked use: ['Merge old stored values because their keys coincide.', 'Discard an old representative during the key-distribution step.']
- **limit-catalytic-excursion-contract** (hypothesis): Restoring catalytic equality requires repeatable endpoint excursions whose paths and results are independent of incoming catalytic contents; nested calls must restore those contents. Blocked use: ['Choose an endpoint using the catalytic bit modified by an earlier excursion.', 'Use the local equality identity as proof that arbitrary nested endpoint procedures restore memory.']
- **limit-numerical-clock-is-not-statistical-budget** (approximation): Increasing the numerical clock approximates the same estimator value; it does not improve that estimator's statistical error. Blocked use: ['Claim arbitrarily accurate acceptance probabilities by requesting later digits without changing the statistical construction.', 'Let output precision change structural lists, port orders or validity conventions.']
- **limit-arithmetic-recipe-contract** (hypothesis): The numerical interface is restricted to its syntactically bounded recipe class, positive reciprocal intervals, defined operand streams and regenerable query-free address computations. Blocked use: ['Apply the reciprocal construction at a possible zero denominator.', 'Retain an operand-dependent coefficient word across a late suffix query.', 'Treat an unbounded incoming rank as an indexed rank over a bounded immediate descriptor domain.']
- **limit-total-controller-environments** (hypothesis): Final enumeration needs terminating digit queries on every environment, including environments where the estimator is inaccurate. Physical input heads must remain confined to the real endmarked input. Blocked use: ['Derive polynomial running time from a space bound without proving termination.', 'Permit inaccurate environments to trigger unbounded recursive queries or off-endmarker physical scans.']
- **limit-enumeration-multiplicities** (hypothesis): Median enumeration must reproduce the original conditional environment law, preserving repeated raw encodings that induce identical reduced fingerprint parameters. Blocked use: ['Deduplicate reduced fingerprint parameters before taking the median.', 'Replace the original conditional multiset by an unweighted set of distinct estimator values.']
- **limit-specified-start-moment-cost** (approximation): An integrated estimator error bound is not the same bound at an arbitrary designated start; selecting that coordinate incurs the stage-size factor. Blocked use: ['Drop the stage-size factor when converting integrated error into a specified-start tail guarantee.']
- **limit-promise-outside-correctness** (formal_scope): The promise separator is total, but correctness is prescribed only on the disjoint yes and no sets. Blocked use: ['Require a specified decision on inputs outside the promise.', 'Infer a procedure deciding membership in the promise itself.']
- **limit-certified-search-probability** (hypothesis): Guaranteed accepting-run extraction requires the stated inverse-polynomial acceptance lower bound and a polynomial time bound on every coin sequence. Mere existence of an accepting run is insufficient for the stated guarantee. Blocked use: ['Claim guaranteed witness discovery for arbitrarily small positive acceptance probability.', 'Output a witness without the premise that every accepting source run certifies the desired relation.']
- **limit-write-only-transducer-output** (formal_scope): Output is not available as work memory, and previously emitted source symbols cannot influence later source transitions in the witness application. Blocked use: ['Store a computation history on the output tape and read it back.', 'Apply the witness guarantee to a source whose transitions inspect its past output.']
- **limit-compiler-supplied-promises** (hypothesis): The effective compiler receives resource parameters as hypotheses; it does not determine whether an arbitrary source satisfies those bounds or its bounded-error promise. Blocked use: ['Use compilation as a semantic verifier of source running time, work space or error probability.', 'Assert language preservation when the supplied source promises fail.']
- **limit-fixed-library-effectivity** (formal_scope): Source-specific compilation is a computable syntactic construction after a valid finite deterministic library has been fixed. It is not a procedure discovering a separator or a space coefficient from an arbitrary machine. Blocked use: ['Treat the compiler as an algorithm for discovering the fixed separator from arbitrary program behavior.', 'Claim a uniform practical compilation-time bound from termination alone.']
- **limit-local-certificate-versus-global-theorem** (formal_scope): A finite check of catalytic flips and reads can establish the local identity on its checked domain, but cannot certify the full estimator, nested excursion implementation or simultaneous controller space bound. Blocked use: ['Promote a bounded local equality check to verification of the main class equality.', 'Treat successful vector restoration as a certificate for all recursive controller interfaces.']

Scope note of family 103 (`lean/docs/103.md`, verbatim):

> The following describes the scope of the Lean formalization related to the following accompanying paper(s):
>
> - [Exact derandomization of logarithmic space: L = RL = BPL](../../preprints/Exact-Derandomization-of-Logarithmic-Space-L-equals-RL-equals-BPL-September-23-2026/paper.pdf)
>
> ## Scope
>
> The formalization proves $\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}$ for binary languages in an explicit Turing-machine model with logarithmic workspace. The randomized classes use polynomial time: $\mathsf{RL}$ never accepts a no-instance and accepts a yes-instance with probability at least $1/2$, while $\mathsf{BPL}$ has acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on yes-instances and at most $1/3$ on no-instances. Thus bounded-error randomness does not enlarge deterministic logarithmic space in this model.
>
> The selected theorem asserts equality of the language classes. The paper's explicit compiler and numerical running-time bounds are not separately stated in this Comparator target.

```lean
import Mathlib

namespace OAI

/-! Exact logarithmic-space derandomization for finite transition-table machines. -/

namespace ExactDerandomization

abbrev Word := List Bool
abbrev Language := Set Word
abbrev CoinTape := ℕ → Bool

inductive Direction where
  | left | stay | right
  deriving DecidableEq

inductive InputSymbol where
  | leftMarker | bit (b : Bool) | rightMarker
  deriving DecidableEq

def Direction.move (d : Direction) (z : ℤ) : ℤ :=
  match d with
  | .left => z - 1
  | .stay => z
  | .right => z + 1

def Direction.moveInput (d : Direction) {n : ℕ} (i : Fin (n + 2)) : Fin (n + 2) :=
  match d with
  | .left => ⟨i.val - 1, lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.sub_le _ _) i.isLt⟩
  | .stay => i
  | .right => ⟨min (i.val + 1) (n + 1), by omega⟩

def readInput (x : Word) (i : Fin (x.length + 2)) : InputSymbol :=
  if i.val = 0 then .leftMarker else
    match x[i.val - 1]? with
    | some b => .bit b
    | none => .rightMarker

structure Action (q w h : ℕ) where
  nextState : Fin (q + 1)
  write : Fin w → Bool
  workMove : Fin w → Direction
  inputMove : Fin h → Direction

structure Machine (q w h : ℕ) where
  initialState : Fin (q + 1)
  output : Fin (q + 1) → Option Bool
  transition : Fin (q + 1) → (Fin h → InputSymbol) → (Fin w → Bool) → Bool →
    Action q w h

structure Configuration (q w h n : ℕ) where
  state : Fin (q + 1)
  inputPos : Fin h → Fin (n + 2)
  workPos : Fin w → ℤ
  work : Fin w → ℤ → Bool

namespace Machine

variable {q w h : ℕ}

def initial (M : Machine q w h) (n : ℕ) : Configuration q w h n where
  state := M.initialState
  inputPos := fun _ => ⟨0, by omega⟩
  workPos := fun _ => 0
  work := fun _ _ => false

def step (M : Machine q w h) (x : Word) (b : Bool)
    (c : Configuration q w h x.length) : Configuration q w h x.length :=
  match M.output c.state with
  | some _ => c
  | none =>
    let a := M.transition c.state (fun j => readInput x (c.inputPos j))
      (fun k => c.work k (c.workPos k)) b
    { state := a.nextState
      inputPos := fun j => (a.inputMove j).moveInput (c.inputPos j)
      workPos := fun k => (a.workMove k).move (c.workPos k)
      work := fun k => Function.update (c.work k) (c.workPos k) (a.write k) }

def run (M : Machine q w h) (x : Word) (coins : CoinTape) :
    ℕ → Configuration q w h x.length
  | 0 => M.initial x.length
  | t + 1 => M.step x (coins t) (M.run x coins t)

def spaceThrough (M : Machine q w h) (x : Word) (coins : CoinTape) (t : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ k : Fin w, ((Finset.range (t + 1)).image
    (fun s => (M.run x coins s).workPos k)).card

def LogSpace (M : Machine q w h) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (x : Word) (coins : CoinTape) (t : ℕ),
    M.spaceThrough x coins t ≤ c * Nat.clog 2 (x.length + 2)

def Deterministic (M : Machine q w h) : Prop :=
  ∀ s i v, M.transition s i v false = M.transition s i v true

def HaltsBy (M : Machine q w h) (x : Word) (t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ coins : CoinTape, ∃ b : Bool, M.output (M.run x coins t).state = some b

def Decides (M : Machine q w h) (A : Language) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Word, ∃ (t : ℕ) (b : Bool),
    (b = true ↔ x ∈ A) ∧ ∀ coins : CoinTape,
      M.output (M.run x coins t).state = some b

def extendCoins {t : ℕ} (bits : Fin t → Bool) : CoinTape :=
  fun s => if hs : s < t then bits ⟨s, hs⟩ else false

def acceptanceProbability (M : Machine q w h) (x : Word) (t : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  ((Finset.univ.filter (fun bits : Fin t → Bool =>
    M.output (M.run x (extendCoins bits) t).state = some true)).card : ℚ) /
    (2 : ℚ) ^ t

end Machine

def polynomialClock (c k n : ℕ) : ℕ := c * (n + 2) ^ k

def L : Set Language :=
  {A | ∃ (q w h : ℕ) (M : Machine q w h),
    M.Deterministic ∧ M.LogSpace ∧ M.Decides A}

def RL : Set Language :=
  {A | ∃ (q w h : ℕ) (M : Machine q w h),
    M.LogSpace ∧ ∃ (c k : ℕ), 0 < c ∧ ∀ x : Word,
      M.HaltsBy x (polynomialClock c k x.length) ∧
      (x ∈ A → (1 / 2 : ℚ) ≤ M.acceptanceProbability x
        (polynomialClock c k x.length)) ∧
      (x ∉ A → M.acceptanceProbability x (polynomialClock c k x.length) = 0)}

def BPL : Set Language :=
  {A | ∃ (q w h : ℕ) (M : Machine q w h),
    M.LogSpace ∧ ∃ (c k : ℕ), 0 < c ∧ ∀ x : Word,
      M.HaltsBy x (polynomialClock c k x.length) ∧
      (x ∈ A → (2 / 3 : ℚ) ≤ M.acceptanceProbability x
        (polynomialClock c k x.length)) ∧
      (x ∉ A → M.acceptanceProbability x (polynomialClock c k x.length) ≤ (1 / 3 : ℚ))}


theorem exact_logarithmic_space_derandomization :
    L = RL ∧ RL = BPL := by
  sorry

end ExactDerandomization

end OAI
```

```json
  },
  "status": "present",
  "toolchain": "leanprover/lean4:v4.34.1"
}
```

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We prove $`\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}`$, resolving the derandomization problem for polynomial-time randomized logarithmic space.

<a id="sec:intro"></a>
### Introduction

A logarithmic-space machine can remember a bounded number of positions in its input, but cannot keep a polynomial-length computation or random tape. Can fresh random bits increase what such a machine can decide? We answer this question by giving a deterministic logarithmic-space simulation of every polynomial-time randomized logarithmic-space computation with bounded error.

We use machines with finite control, an endmarked read-only input, finitely many work tapes, and fresh independent fair bits. Input heads are confined between the endmarkers. All randomized running-time bounds hold on every random tape. Space counts traversed writable cells in bits, including every simultaneously live counter, numerical register and suspended call; visiting a blank work cell counts toward space. A transducer has a one-way write-only output tape. Throughout, $n$ is the input length and logarithms have base two.

The class $\mathsf L$ consists of languages decidable by deterministic machines in $O(\log(n+2))$ work space. Such a halting deterministic machine has only polynomially many configurations and hence runs in polynomial time. The class $\mathsf{RL}$ permits polynomial-time randomized machines in this space, with acceptance probability zero on no inputs and at least $1/2$ on yes inputs. For $\mathsf{BPL}$, the corresponding probabilities are at most $1/3$ and at least $2/3$.

<a id="stmt-thm-main"></a>
<div id="thm:main" class="theorem">

**Theorem 1** (Exact logarithmic-space derandomization). *$$\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}.$$*

</div>

The proof approximates arbitrary acceptance probabilities. This gives the two-sided statement directly, and also applies to computations whose acceptance probabilities have no decision gap. Its quantitative form separates the memory needed for the input from the memory needed for the requested accuracy.

<a id="stmt-thm-probability"></a>
<div id="thm:probability" class="theorem">

**Theorem 2** (Acceptance-probability approximation). *Fix a randomized machine $\mathcal M$ with polynomial worst-case running time and $O(\log(n+2))$ work space. Let $p_{\mathcal M}(x)$ be its acceptance probability on an input $x$ of length $n$. There is a uniform deterministic algorithm which, on input $(x,1^q)$ with $q\ge1$, outputs an integer $0\le a\le2^{q+2}$ satisfying $$\left|a2^{-(q+2)}-p_{\mathcal M}(x)\right|\le2^{-q}.$$ It uses $O(\log(n+2)+q)$ work space and $(n+2)^{O(1)}2^{O(q)}$ time. The constants depend only on $\mathcal M$.*

</div>

In particular, every fixed inverse-polynomial accuracy is attained in logarithmic space and polynomial time. The precision parameter is unary; the running-time bound is exponential in general $q$. We first prove the fixed inverse-polynomial result and then obtain the single variable-precision algorithm by padding. Section <a href="#sec:conclusion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:conclusion">12</a> also derives total deterministic separators for bounded-error promise problems and constructs accepting runs when the machine’s acceptance probability has a specified inverse-polynomial lower bound.

The simulation is also effective at the level of machine descriptions. Given a source program and supplied polynomial-time and logarithmic-space bounds, one terminating compiler produces a deterministic decider and explicit numerical bounds for its space and time (Theorem <a href="#thm:effective-simulation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:effective-simulation">74</a>). The supplied bounds are hypotheses on the source, rather than properties the compiler must decide. Section <a href="#sec:compiler" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:compiler">13</a> constructs this compiler by specializing one fixed deterministic library.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### Historical context

The complexity of probabilistic Turing machines was developed by Gill (Gill 1977) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[Gill1977](#ref-Gill1977)], including measures of both time and tape usage. Random walks made the logarithmic-space question concrete: Aleliunas, Karp, Lipton, Lovász and Rackoff obtained polynomial-time randomized algorithms for undirected connectivity and explicitly asked whether polynomial-time randomized logarithmic space could be simulated in deterministic logarithmic space (Aleliunas et al. 1979) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[AleliunasKLLR1979](#ref-AleliunasKLLR1979)]. Early work also studied probabilistic machines without a polynomial-time restriction. Borodin, Cook and Pippenger obtained a quadratic-space deterministic simulation in this broader setting (Borodin, Cook, and Pippenger 1983) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[BorodinCookPippenger1983](#ref-BorodinCookPippenger1983)]. The distinction between a space bound and simultaneous time and space bounds is essential throughout this history.

Pseudorandom generators attack the problem by replacing a long sequence of fresh random bits with the output generated from a short seed. Ajtai, Komlós and Szemerédi gave early logarithmic-space constructions that hit small-space tests using short random strings (Ajtai, Komlós, and Szemerédi 1987) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[AjtaiKomlosSzemeredi1987](#ref-AjtaiKomlosSzemeredi1987)]. Babai, Nisan and Szegedy subsequently obtained pseudorandom generators through multiparty communication bounds (Babai, Nisan, and Szegedy 1992) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[BabaiNisanSzegedy1992](#ref-BabaiNisanSzegedy1992)]. Nisan’s generator uses $O(S\log R)$ seed bits for a space-$S$ computation reading $R$ random bits (Nisan 1992) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[Nisan1992](#ref-Nisan1992)]. For logarithmic space and polynomially many bits this gives $O(\log^2 n)$ seed length; direct seed enumeration has a quasipolynomial time bound. Nisan’s later simultaneous simulation achieves polynomial time and $O(\log^2 n)$ space (Nisan 1994) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[Nisan1994RLinSC](#ref-Nisan1994RLinSC)]. Although its title uses $\mathrm{RL}$, that result includes two-sided bounded error. For $S(n)\ge\log n$, Nisan and Zuckerman showed that a space-$S$ computation using $\operatorname{poly}(S)$ random bits can be simulated using only $O(S)$ random bits and $O(S)$ space (Nisan and Zuckerman 1996) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[NisanZuckerman1996](#ref-NisanZuckerman1996)]. The restriction on the original number of random bits is substantive; for logarithmic space it permits polylogarithmically many bits.

Saks and Zhou reduced the deterministic space needed for general bounded-error logarithmic-space computation to $O(\log^{3/2}n)$ (Saks and Zhou 1999) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[SaksZhou1999](#ref-SaksZhou1999)]. Cai, Chakaravarthy and van Melkebeek established a simultaneous tradeoff: for each fixed rational $0\le\alpha\le1/2$, the simulation uses time $n^{O(\log^{1/2-\alpha}n)}$ and space $O(\log^{3/2+\alpha}n)$ (Cai, Chakaravarthy, and Melkebeek 2006) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[CaiChakaravarthyVanMelkebeek2006](#ref-CaiChakaravarthyVanMelkebeek2006)]. The polynomial-time endpoint has squared-logarithmic space. Hoza subsequently improved the general space bound to $O(\log^{3/2}n/\sqrt{\log\log n})$ (Hoza 2021, Theorem 1.6 and Corollary A.5) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[Hoza2021](#ref-Hoza2021)]. These smaller space containments do not assert the same polynomial-time endpoint. Hoza’s work also develops weighted pseudorandomness, in which signed or real weights replace an ordinary probability distribution; the space-containment improvement and the new weighted-generator construction are distinct results of that paper.

Acceptance-probability estimation also connects derandomization to stochastic matrix products and inverses. Ahmadinejad, Kelner, Murtagh, Peebles, Sidford and Vadhan developed high-precision small-space algorithms for random-walk probabilities, with stronger bounds for Eulerian graphs (Ahmadinejad et al. 2020) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[AhmadinejadKelnerMurtaghPeeblesSidfordVadhan2020](#ref-AhmadinejadKelnerMurtaghPeeblesSidfordVadhan2020)]. Cohen, Doron, Sberlo and Ta-Shma later used varying precision across recursion to improve the space complexity of long stochastic matrix products (Cohen et al. 2023) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[CohenDoronSberloTaShma2023](#ref-CohenDoronSberloTaShma2023)]. The construction below works with a finite inverse on a time-layered configuration graph; its correction and copy hierarchy controls the information retained while individual entries are evaluated.

Structural restrictions on a computation provide another route. For undirected connectivity, Nisan, Szemerédi and Wigderson obtained deterministic space $O(\log^{3/2}n)$ (Nisan, Szemerédi, and Wigderson 1992) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[NisanSzemerediWigderson1992](#ref-NisanSzemerediWigderson1992)], subsequently improved to $O(\log^{4/3}n)$ by Armoni, Ta-Shma, Wigderson and Zhou (Armoni et al. 2000) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[ArmoniTaShmaWigdersonZhou2000](#ref-ArmoniTaShmaWigdersonZhou2000)]. Reingold’s logarithmic-space algorithm, whose conference version appeared at STOC 2005, settles undirected connectivity (Reingold 2005, 2008) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[Reingold2005](#ref-Reingold2005), [Reingold2008](#ref-Reingold2008)]. Reingold, Trevisan and Vadhan studied regular directed graphs and gave logarithmic-space path search for Eulerian directed graphs (Reingold, Trevisan, and Vadhan 2006) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[RTV2006](#ref-RTV2006)]. Their oblivious walk constructions impose additional labeling conditions. General directed configuration graphs need not have these properties, so those results did not settle the unrestricted randomized computation problem. A read-once branching program is a layered deterministic computation that reads the input symbols once in a fixed order (bits in the binary case). Its length is the number of steps, and its width is the largest number of states in a layer. A $1/2$-hitting set for a class of programs contains an accepting input for every member that accepts at least half of all input strings. The relation between one-sided and two-sided derandomization also requires care. Cheng and Hoza proved that one uniformly logarithmic-space-enumerable $1/2$-hitting-set family for all width-$n$, length-$n$ read-once branching programs would yield $\mathsf L=\mathsf{BPL}$ (Cheng and Hoza 2022) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[ChengHoza2022](#ref-ChengHoza2022)]. The premise is a hitting-set construction; it is not merely the language-class equality $\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf L$.

Recent results refine both general and structured models. Chen, Cohen, Doron, Khaskelberg and Ta-Shma improve error reduction for weighted generators; in the polynomial-width regime their construction has seed length $\log|\Sigma|+O(\log^2 T+\log(1/\delta))$, where $T$ is branching-program length, $\Sigma$ its alphabet and $\delta$ the error (Chen et al. 2026) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[ChenCohenDoronKhaskelbergTaShma2026](#ref-ChenCohenDoronKhaskelbergTaShma2026)]. Cheng and Wu obtain simultaneous polynomial-time and polylogarithmic-space simulations for regular branching programs, with extensions to polynomial-time randomized logarithmic-space machines whose two-way read-only random tape visits each cell at most constantly often, and to such machines with read-once randomness and an auxiliary stack whose push, pop and idle schedule is independent of the random bits. Consecutive stays on a random-tape cell count as one visit (Cheng and Wu 2026, Theorems 5–6) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[ChengWu2026SC](#ref-ChengWu2026SC)]. Hardness-versus-randomness approaches additionally give conditional, certified and per-instance alternatives; Pyne and Tell survey this line of work (Pyne and Tell 2026) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[PyneTell2026](#ref-PyneTell2026)].

Effectivity has its own substantial antecedents. Pyne, Raz and Zhan construct a universal deterministic estimator whose $O(S(n))$ space guarantee follows from $\mathsf{prBPL}\subseteq\mathsf{SPACE}[O(S(n))]$, for space-constructible $S(n)\ge\log n$ (Pyne, Raz, and Zhan 2023, full version, Theorem 5.1) <a id="pm-cite-22"></a>[[PyneRazZhan2023](#ref-PyneRazZhan2023)]. Here $\mathsf{prBPL}$ denotes promise problems solvable in polynomial time and randomized logarithmic space with bounded error. The compiler below uses a fixed separator established in this paper and supplies explicit source-specific numerical resource bounds. Its construction should be read in this context of universal simulation, with the source bounds supplied as part of the compiler input.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### Proof strategy

Fix a randomized machine and an input of length $n$, and write $B=\Theta(\log(n+2))$. The proof constructs a finite family of estimates of its acceptance probability, indexed by $O(B)$-bit descriptions. More than three quarters of these estimates are accurate; every member of the family can be evaluated by a halting deterministic computation using $O(B)$ space. Exhaustive enumeration then gives a deterministic answer. The second guarantee is essential: enumeration must finish even on choices for which the estimate is inaccurate.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
###### The exact target.

The configuration reduction of Section <a href="#sec:model" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:model">2</a> gives a strictly forward substochastic matrix $S$ on a polynomial-size set $V_0$ and a vector $e\in\{0,1\}^{V_0}$ indicating accepting final configurations. The vector $$p_0=(I-S)^{-1}e$$ records acceptance probabilities from all configurations. The inverse is a finite sum, because every transition advances time. Section <a href="#sec:hierarchy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:hierarchy">4</a> replaces $S$ successively by transitions $C_l$ on sets $V_l$ of configuration copies, carrying accumulated rewards $W_l\in[0,1]^{V_l}$. Each copy step has a designated primary copy. If $z_l$ is obtained from the original start $x_0$ by always choosing that copy, then $$0\le p_0(x_0)-W_l(z_l)
                    \le |V_0|\,2^{-(H-1)l},$$ where $H\ge4$ is fixed. Thus $L=O(B)$ stages make $W_L(z_L)$ accurate to any fixed inverse-polynomial error. Every stage has at most $N=2^{C_NB}$ vertices for a fixed constant $C_N$.

<a id="pm-h-6"></a>
###### From the estimator to a deterministic decision.

The algorithm estimates $W_L$ in one shared finite random environment $\sigma$. Its law is uniform on a specified finite set of matrix-and-bit-string encodings of length $O(B)$. On each channel a retention test selects vertices; write $X_f(v)$ for the indicator that $v$ is retained at the final stage rate $f=2^{-HL}$, and $\pi_f$ for its probability. Section <a href="#sec:env" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:env">3</a> gives $\pi_f\asymp f$. Theorem <a href="#thm:fp-estimators" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:fp-estimators">46</a> proves, for the actual estimator $\bar W_L$, $$\frac1N\mathbb E_\sigma\sum_{v\in V_L}\frac{X_f(v)}f
          |\bar W_L(v)-W_L(v)|^8\le C^8 2^{-8p}.$$ Here $p$ is the statistical accuracy exponent. Keeping only the summand at $z_L$ gives $$\mathbb E\!\left[|\bar W_L(z_L)-W_L(z_L)|^8
                     \mid X_f(z_L)=1\right]
       \le N\frac f{\pi_f}C^8 2^{-8p}.$$ The factor $N$ is the price of passing from the integrated bound to one specified start. Since $\log N=O(B)$, taking the estimator’s statistical budget to be a sufficiently large fixed multiple of $B$ makes $p$ large enough to pay this price and gives an accurate value on more than three quarters of the conditional environments.

The implementation computes dyadic approximations to the same fixed value $\bar W_L(z_L)$ on every environment. Numerical precision changes the requested digits, not the lists and ports defining that value. Choosing the stage count, statistical budget and digit accuracy makes the total error less than $1/8$ on more than three quarters of the encodings conditioned on $X_f(z_L)=1$. Their median has the same error bound. We enumerate the original encodings with their original multiplicities, so the multiset reproduces exactly this conditional law.

Repeated enumeration finds the median while retaining only the current encoding and $O(B)$-bit numerical and counting registers. Every digit query used here requests one of the first $O(B)$ binary places, terminates in $O(B)$ space, and confines its physical input heads between the real endmarkers. It therefore has only $2^{O(B)}$ complete configurations and takes at most that many steps. There are also $2^{O(B)}$ encodings, so the entire computation takes polynomial time. Comparing its answer with $1/2$ distinguishes acceptance probabilities at most $1/3$ from those at least $2/3$. This proves the nontrivial containment in Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a>.

<a id="pm-h-7"></a>
###### Why the hierarchy can be estimated.

The hierarchy reduces transition entries more rapidly than it increases the number of vertices incident to positive entries. A correction $E$ replaces $C$ by $D=C-E+EC$, with $$I-D=(I+E)(I-C).$$ This identity transfers the removed transition contribution into the reward. Detectors identify columns with many substantial entries and suppress correction there. The copy step distributes the remaining large entries while controlling how many vertices are incident to them. An ordered-support argument gives a factorial truncation bound, so only constantly many correction steps are needed at each stage.

The exact matrices and conditional expectations define the targets; they are not stored. Section <a href="#sec:atom" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:atom">5</a> represents their contributions by sample-dependent tables with bounded row support. Corrections also have bounded incoming degree. Their true conditional means recover the required entries. The algorithm substitutes earlier estimates into these formulas, so the analysis must bound the resulting bias without assuming that the estimated factors are independent. Conditional averaging preserves the specified source and endpoint retention tests. Its uniform mixing bound is derived from classical property (T) results of Shalom (Shalom 1999) <a id="pm-cite-23"></a>[[Shalom1999](#ref-Shalom1999)]; Section <a href="#sec:averaging" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:averaging">6</a> proves the finite-action and sampling consequences used here.

At parent budget $M$, Section <a href="#sec:est" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:est">7</a> averages differences between child estimates at consecutive budgets $m$ and $m-1$. These differences have small norm because both approximate the same true sample term. Their contributions at the same endpoint are combined before measuring the difference. The slack $M-m$ has two roles: it determines the length of conditional averaging available to reduce the noise, and it bounds the description of an immediate sample path. Grouping comparable slacks lets Section <a href="#sec:buf-compression" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:buf-compression">8</a> replace each row array by a short list of exceptions to a common default. The proof charges deterministic conditional-mean error separately from residual noise.

A product follows a correction edge to an intermediate vertex and then queries a right factor there. Releasing the old source changes the weighted error domain. Bounded incoming degree controls that change, and the task’s accuracy assignment pays the resulting factor. Thus the same construction that permits a source address to be discarded also appears explicitly in the error analysis.

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
###### Why the lists fit in logarithmic space.

A list entry is found by a path. Retaining a full endpoint at every recursive level would cost too much. Section <a href="#sec:fp-blocks" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:fp-blocks">9</a> therefore compares endpoints by short fingerprint keys at small slacks, combining polynomial evaluation and affine hashing (Schwartz 1980; Carter and Wegman 1979) <a id="pm-cite-24"></a>[[Schwartz1980](#ref-Schwartz1980), [CarterWegman1979](#ref-CarterWegman1979)]. Candidate endpoints can depend on earlier comparisons, so a fixed-pair collision estimate alone is insufficient. A comparison calculation using exact equality within one budget block produces candidate sets independent of that block’s fingerprint bits. Smooth support functions charge paths that leave these sets to lower-call errors; collisions within the fixed sets supply the remaining error. This coupled induction proves the moment bound for the actual estimator.

Sections <a href="#sec:arith" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:arith">10</a> and <a href="#sec:ctrl" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:ctrl">11</a> establish its total space bound. Numerical operations request one bounded digit at a time. The controller keeps one vertex cursor, uses bounded inverse ports for correction moves, and recovers incoming accesses by traversing finite program trees, using the contour idea of Cook and McKenzie (Cook and McKenzie 1987) <a id="pm-cite-25"></a>[[CookMcKenzie1987](#ref-CookMcKenzie1987)] and the space-preserving traversal perspective of Lange, McKenzie and Tapp (Lange, McKenzie, and Tapp 2000) <a id="pm-cite-26"></a>[[LMT2000](#ref-LMT2000)]. A shared catalytic bit vector permits fingerprint comparisons without keeping a key index at every recursive level. The controller assigns each call a decreasing recursion allowance $w$, with top allowance $O(B)$, and uses the requested digit place $t$ as its numerical clock. If the child has allowance $w'$ and digit place $j$, all local data retained during that call occupy at most $$A(w-w')+D(t-j)$$ bits, including the controller copies used by a traversal. The child clock may increase only in proportion to the decrease of allowance. These differences telescope along the active call chain; the environment, cursor, catalyst and scratch are shared once. The bound and termination do not depend on statistical accuracy.

Section <a href="#sec:conclusion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:conclusion">12</a> carries out the median construction for fixed inverse-polynomial error and derives the class equality and promise separation. It then obtains one algorithm for all unary precision requests by padding, and constructs certified accepting computations when the machine’s acceptance probability has an inverse-polynomial lower bound. Section <a href="#sec:compiler" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:compiler">13</a> is a separate application of fixed-precision approximation: one resource-capped universal interpreter yields a fixed deterministic library, whose syntactic specialization supplies explicit resource bounds for each source machine.

<a id="sec:model"></a>
### The transition model and resource parameters

We first express acceptance probability as a finite matrix inverse. Time labels make the transition matrix nilpotent; keeping the complete configuration at each vertex gives local access in both directions. The construction will use the resulting probability vector at every configuration, as well as its value at the designated start.

A matrix indexed by a finite set $V$ is *strictly forward* if there is an integer time attached to every vertex and every nonzero entry goes to a strictly later time. It is *substochastic* if its entries are nonnegative and each row sums to at most one. An edge is specified by a vertex and a port from a fixed finite set. A *paired* edge operation returns the other endpoint together with its inverse port; applying the inverse operation restores the first endpoint. Absent ports are explicitly recognized.

<a id="stmt-lem-model-reduction"></a>
<div id="lem:model-reduction" class="lemma">

**Lemma 3** (Configuration reduction). *Fix a polynomial-time randomized machine using $O(\log(n+2))$ work space. On an input of length $n$ one can specify, uniformly in logarithmic space, a polynomial-size vertex set $V_0$, a strictly forward substochastic matrix $S$, a vector $e\in\{0,1\}^{V_0}$, and a start vertex $x_0$ with the following properties.*

1.  *The incoming and outgoing port degrees of $S$ are bounded by constants depending only on the machine. Port validity, edge weights, and pairing are computable in logarithmic space.*

2.  *The vector $p_0=(I-S)^{-1}e$ is well defined and belongs to $[0,1]^{V_0}$.*

3.  *The coordinate $p_0(x_0)$ is the acceptance probability of the machine.*

*In particular, an $\mathsf{RL}$ computation gives the promise $p_0(x_0)=0$ or $p_0(x_0)\ge1/2$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-model-reduction"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-model-reduction</summary>

*Proof.* Let $T(n)$ be a fixed polynomial upper bound on the running time. A vertex records a time in $\{0,\ldots,T(n)\}$, the finite control, all input and work head positions, and the contents of a sufficiently large box of $O(\log(n+2))$ work cells. Take elementary machine steps with fixed dyadic coin probabilities. A transition advances the time by one. Invalid configurations or moves leaving the box have no corresponding transition. The box is chosen large enough that this never affects a computation from the specified start.

Each elementary step has constantly many successor choices. To find predecessors, guess the old finite control, locally overwritten symbols, head movements, and coin choice, then check that the forward step gives the specified configuration. There are constantly many such guesses. Combine transitions with the same ordered pair of endpoints by adding their probabilities. Order the distinct successors and predecessors by their configuration encodings; their positions give paired ports for the resulting matrix entries. These lists have constant length, so duplicate removal, summed weights, and the inverse port are computed in logarithmic space by local enumeration. This base computation makes no recursive graph queries. All records use $O(\log(n+2))$ bits, and the read-only input can be consulted during these checks.

All input-head coordinates in the vertex universe are restricted to a fixed polynomial interval containing the positions reachable within $T(n)$ local steps from their specified initial positions. Configurations and predecessor candidates outside that interval are invalid. To obtain a simulated head’s scanned symbol, compare its stored coordinate with the input boundaries, supply any required endmarker or off-data blank according to the source tape convention, and otherwise scan the real endmarked input to the designated position using a logarithmic-space counter. A position forbidden by the source tape convention remains invalid. The physical scan stays between the real endmarkers, even when a valid simulated coordinate is outside the data. This routine makes no recursive graph query.

An already halted computation keeps its complete tape and head data while its time advances. In particular, halted configurations are not merged into a single vertex. Let $e$ be one precisely at accepting configurations at time $T(n)$, and zero elsewhere. Final-time rows have no outgoing transitions. Thus $S$ is strictly forward and substochastic, and it is nilpotent. Its inverse expression is the finite sum $$(I-S)^{-1}e=\sum_{j=0}^{T(n)}S^je.$$ Starting from any valid configuration, at most one reward can be collected, at final time. The sum is therefore a probability in $[0,1]$. At $x_0$ it is exactly the machine’s acceptance probability. ◻

</details>

The coordinatewise bound on $p_0$ will be used after weighted projections to larger vertex sets. It holds at every configuration, independently of the acceptance probability at the designated start. Thus the matrix construction and the probability approximation below apply to arbitrary randomized computations satisfying the resource bounds.

<a id="pm-h-10"></a>
###### Size convention.

Fix an integer parameter $B$, a power of two, comparable with $\log_2(n+2)$ and at least a sufficiently large fixed constant. For example, take the least power of two at least the maximum of that constant and $\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil$. This choice is computable in logarithmic space and includes all bounded input lengths in the same construction. All constants throughout the construction are independent of the input; they may depend on the fixed machine and, for fixed inverse-polynomial accuracy, its fixed exponent. The uniform precision parameter of Theorem <a href="#thm:probability" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:probability">2</a> is handled separately by padding. The number of stages is $L=O(B)$. At stage $l$, a vertex has a base identifier followed by $l$ symbols from a fixed radix $D_0$. The radix will be selected by the hierarchy. Encode each base vertex by a fixed-width radix-$D_0$ word and prepend the digit $1$; unused base words are invalid. Appending one copy digit at each stage gives injective numerical identifiers even across different stage lengths. Indeed, a base width $w$ places stage-$l$ identifiers in $[D_0^{w+l},2D_0^{w+l})$, and these intervals are disjoint. Appending a fixed suffix is an affine map on identifiers.

Every stage has size at most a common bound $$N=2^{C_NB}.$$ We may increase the fixed constant $C_N$ as needed. This is a bound on one stage, not a claim that there are only $N$ pairs of vertices. Integrated entry errors below carry a factor $1/N$ while summing over both endpoints.

Fix integers $H\ge4$ and $2\le h_0<H$, and put $$b_k=2^{-Hk}\qquad(k\ge0).$$ These are the nominal sampling rates. Stage $l$ will have density $f=b_l$. The stochastic tables will use rates from this same grid for their source and terminal retention tests. The error power in the later analysis is always $s=8$.

<a id="pm-h-11"></a>
###### Uniform constants and finite ranges.

All thresholds needed by the algorithm can be chosen rational, with fixed gaps, and all discrete constants can be chosen integer. We first prove estimates with constants uniform in the ambient finite universe. The sampling construction applies to every finite range of identifiers and rates once its prime field is sufficiently large. The hierarchy uses $O(B)$ copy digits and rates with $k=O(B)$; Section <a href="#subsec:final-constants" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="subsec:final-constants">12.1</a> will verify this rate bound also for the recursive estimator and give a compatible order of constant choices.

We can then take the prime field to have size $2^{O(B)}$, with its exponent chosen after these constants. Its elements and all identifiers occupy $O(B)$ bits. Increasing that exponent does not change the probabilistic constants proved in the next section.

<a id="sec:env"></a>
### Rank channels for retained vertex sets

The hierarchy will use random retained sets to detect columns with many substantial entries. The atom construction will use the same sets to represent matrix entries. We define the sampling channels and prove the marginal, conditional-pair, and count estimates needed for these two constructions. Section <a href="#sec:averaging" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:averaging">6</a> later constructs averaging walks that preserve specified retention conditions.

The environment consists of the independent rank channels below together with a finite string of independent uniform auxiliary bits. The length and uses of that string will be specified when needed.

We use a fixed number of independent rank channels, including channels denoted $X,Y,Z$. Extra channels, when needed, are also a fixed finite number. A channel is a uniformly random matrix $$A=(a_0,F)\in\mathbb F_P^{H\times h_0}$$ conditioned on the last $r=h_0-1$ columns $F$ being linearly independent. We call such an ordered collection of columns a *frame*. The integer $P$ is prime. It is chosen larger than every identifier and sufficiently large for all rate comparisons below. For a numerical identifier $y$, set $$v(y)=(1,y,\ldots,y^{h_0-1})^{\mathsf T},
\qquad a(y)=Av(y)\in\mathbb F_P^H.$$ Field elements in a retention test use their representatives in $\{0,\ldots,P-1\}$. At nominal rate $b_k$, let $$L_k=\lceil P2^{-k}\rceil,\qquad
\pi_{b_k}=(L_k/P)^H.$$ The identifier is retained if all coordinates of $a(y)$ lie in $\{0,\ldots,L_k-1\}$. Write $X_a(y)$ for the indicator on channel $X$ at rate $a$, and similarly for other channels. The same notation permits a specified fixed suffix in the channel argument. Retention boxes are nested. All rates in this section belong to the grid $b_k=2^{-Hk}$, and the admissible range satisfies $P2^{-k}\ge1$. The choices of $H,h_0$ and the identifier range are those of Section <a href="#sec:model" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:model">2</a>.

<a id="stmt-lem-env-ranks"></a>
<div id="lem:env-ranks" class="lemma">

**Lemma 4** (Rank-channel estimates). *There are positive constants $c_\pi,C_\pi,C_{\rm pair},C_{\rm var}$, depending only on $H,h_0$, with the following properties in every admissible finite range.*

1.  *A specified identifier is retained at rate $a$ with probability $\pi_a$, where $c_\pi a\le\pi_a\le C_\pi a$.*

2.  *For distinct identifiers $x,y$ and any admissible rates $u,a$, $$\Pr\{X_a(y)=1\mid X_u(x)=1\}\le C_{\rm pair}a.$$*

3.  *If $A_0$ is a deterministic set of $q$ distinct identifiers and $T_a=\sum_{y\in A_0}X_a(y)$, then $$\Pr\{T_a<q\pi_a/2\}\le \frac{C_{\rm var}}{q\pi_a}
    \quad(q>0).$$*

4.  *Replacing every channel argument $y$ by the same injective affine map $\alpha y+\beta$ leaves the joint law of all evaluations unchanged, provided $\alpha\ne0$ in $\mathbb F_P$. In particular, a common fixed padding suffix leaves their law unchanged.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-env-ranks"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-env-ranks</summary>

*Proof.* The probability that an unrestricted $H$-by-$r$ matrix is a frame is $$q_{\rm fr}=\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}(1-P^{j-H})\ge c_{\rm fr}>0.$$ For fixed positive-degree coefficients, $a_0$ is uniform, so any one evaluation is uniform in $\mathbb F_P^H$ and independent of frame success. This proves the exact marginal retention probability. In the ranges used, take $P2^{-k}\ge1$. Then $P2^{-k}\le L_k\le2P2^{-k}$, proving comparability. The prime exponent can in fact make all these sides much larger than one.

Without conditioning on a frame, two evaluations at distinct field points are independent uniform vectors: the two evaluation functionals have rank two since $h_0\ge2$. Consequently $$\Pr\{X_a(y)=1,X_u(x)=1\mid F\text{ is a frame}\}
\le \frac{\pi_a\pi_u}{q_{\rm fr}}.$$ The first marginal after conditioning is still $\pi_u$, which proves the second assertion.

For the third assertion, in the unrestricted distribution the hit count has mean $q\pi_a$ and variance at most $q\pi_a$, by pairwise independence. Chebyshev’s inequality bounds the stated lower-tail event by $4/(q\pi_a)$. Conditioning on frame success increases this probability by at most $1/q_{\rm fr}$.

Finally, substituting $\alpha y+\beta$ in a polynomial acts on its positive-degree coefficient columns by an invertible triangular matrix, with diagonal $\alpha,\ldots,\alpha^{h_0-1}$. It therefore preserves the frame condition. Its action on the full coefficient array is an invertible linear change of variables, so it preserves uniform measure conditional on that condition. Appending digits in radix $D_0$ has $\alpha$ a power of $D_0$; taking $P>D_0$ ensures the required invertibility. ◻

</details>

<a id="sec:hierarchy"></a>
### The exact correction and copy hierarchy

At each stage we reduce the transition entries and transfer their contribution to a reward. The algebra behind this transfer is simple. Given a transition matrix $C$ and a nonnegative correction $E$, put $$D=C-E+EC.$$ Then $I-D=(I+E)(I-C)$. Thus a relation $W=(I-C)p$ becomes $(I+E)W=(I-D)p$: the same vector $p$ is represented by the new transition and the updated reward. The correction must make $D$ nonnegative and keep its row sums at most one. It must also reduce entries sufficiently fast that, after a controlled increase in the number of active vertices, the remaining transition contribution becomes small. The construction uses only the model reduction, with no one-sided acceptance promise.

At one stage the input is a finite ordered set $V$, a rate $0<f\le1$ on the grid of Section <a href="#sec:env" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:env">3</a>, and a nonnegative matrix $C$ with <a id="eq:hier-input"></a>$$C(x,y)=0\quad\text{unless }x<y,\qquad
 C\mathbf1\le\mathbf1,\qquad C(x,y)\le f.
 \label{eq:hier-input}$$ All matrix and vector inequalities are entrywise. Write $$\mathcal R(C)=\{x:\text{some }C(x,y)>0\},\quad
 \mathcal T(C)=\{y:\text{some }C(x,y)>0\},\quad
 \mathcal A(C)=\mathcal R(C)\cup\mathcal T(C).$$ The stage will reduce the entry bound from $f$ to $f/2^H$ and increase $|\mathcal A(C)|$ by at most a factor of two. We first analyze the correction with an arbitrary fixed column multiplier. We then choose that multiplier by a finite detector calculation, and use copies to divide the entries in columns where correction is not fully enabled.

<a id="pm-h-14"></a>
#### Correction with a fixed column multiplier

<a id="eq:hier-Q"></a>
Put $q=2^H$. Fix rational numbers $0<\theta_1<\theta_2<q^{-1}/32$ and a nondecreasing Lipschitz function $Q:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ satisfying $$(t-\theta_2)_+\leq Q(t)\leq(t-\theta_1)_+.
 \label{eq:hier-Q}$$ Its eighth root is required to be Lipschitz on bounded intervals. Here and below the scalar cutoffs can be chosen piecewise polynomial with rational coefficients. To see this explicitly, let $\beta$ be the normalized integral of $t^7(1-t)^7$ on $[0,1]$, extended by zero to the left and one to the right. Both $\beta^{1/8}$ and $(1-\beta)^{1/8}$ are Lipschitz: near their vanishing endpoints the corresponding functions vanish to order eight, and away from those endpoints the assertion follows by differentiation. For example, $$Q(t)=(t-\theta_1)_+
       \beta\left(\frac{t-\theta_1}{\theta_2-\theta_1}\right)$$ has all the stated properties. Near $\theta_1$ its eighth root is of order $(t-\theta_1)_+^{9/8}$; elsewhere its root has bounded derivative on every bounded interval. Let $L_Q$ be a fixed Lipschitz constant for $Q$. For real arguments, extend $Q$ by $Q(t)=0$ when $t<0$. This extension preserves its Lipschitz and root-Lipschitz properties and permits evaluation on real approximations. The exact hierarchy itself uses only nonnegative arguments.

<a id="eq:hier-fixed-g-iteration"></a>
Fix a column multiplier $g:V\to[0,1]$. Starting from zero, define $$E_0=0,\qquad G'_i=C+E_{i-1}C,\qquad
 E_i(x,y)=fQ(G'_i(x,y)/f)g(y)\quad(i\ge1).
 \label{eq:hier-fixed-g-iteration}$$ The cutoff leaves a positive residual at each corrected entry. Keeping $g$ fixed makes the update map monotone. We next show that a fixed number of iterations suffices for every such multiplier, independently of the size of $V$. At a nonnegative fixed point $E_*$ of this recurrence, put $T=C-E_*+E_*C$. In a column with $g(y)=1$, the lower bound on $Q$ gives $T(x,y)\le\theta_2f$. The truncation estimate below will transfer this entry bound to a finite correction, with a small additional error. The fixed point is only a comparison object; the hierarchy will use a finite iteration.

<a id="stmt-lem-hier-fixed-point"></a>
<div id="lem:hier-fixed-point" class="lemma">

<a id="eq:hier-fixed-point"></a>
<a id="eq:hier-factorial"></a>
